finding: Treats MAX cash exposure as split evenly in the CFM JV and uses Safran's disclosed figure as the gauge for GE's own share.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: when I think about David's business, it really is GE, right? Again, there's no better business that we have. So to do something like sell the business to pay a special dividend that strikes at the core of who we are ... making sure that David and his team have the support and the investment
finding: Rejects selling Aviation (to Boeing or anyone) for a payout; Aviation is the core to fund, not a source of cash.
trigger: Shareholder suggested selling Aviation to Boeing for a special dividend, or acquiring Pratt & Whitney.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Cash flow, going to be negative this year. What we said in March is probably going to be breakeven to possibly a negative $2 billion. It's still tough for me to say that out loud.
finding: Delivers bad news plainly and owns the discomfort, without spin.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Our LEAP engine, as many of you know, is underwing on the Boeing 737 MAX, so we're working very closely with our friends at Boeing to get that plane back up in the air, but rest assured as Boeing does, we believe our first mission in that instance is a safe return to flight
finding: Aligns publicly with Boeing and puts safe return to flight ahead of the financial cost to LEAP-1B.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Let's declare clearly what are the most important things we need to do, today, this quarter, this year? What do we need to postpone? What are we not going to do?
finding: Forces explicit trade-offs, including what to postpone and what not to do, to counter GE's habit of over-reach.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Aviation, we have no better business in all of GE than Aviation.
finding: Ranks Aviation as GE's best business, the crown jewel to protect.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: But when a market ticks down and you don't call that early -- you've got a cost structure from the market when it's here -- tough to make money when the market's here, right? ... we made a big bet just as the market was resetting with Alstom.
finding: Draws the lesson from Power: call market downturns early and size costs to the lower market; he is wary of big bets at cycle turns.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: And for our business leaders that's really all about making sure that they end up being paid on the back of what they do with their businesses. All the while the senior team having more of their compensation at risk. As the stock goes, so goes our compensation.
finding: Ties business-leader pay to their own P&L and puts the senior team's pay at risk with the share price.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: A lot of work here as we ramp LEAP in 2019, I think we've got 1,800 engines on tap, clearly moving well with Boeing -- or excuse me, with Airbus. Working closely with Boeing to safely get the MAX back up in the air.
finding: Plans about 1,800 LEAP deliveries for 2019 and notes the Airbus side is moving well while Boeing's is disrupted by the grounding.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: as those opportunities and options materialize, I think folks should rest assure, we're going to be quick to seize them. But not prematurely and not at shareholders' expense.
finding: Portfolio moves are opportunistic but disciplined: fast when value is clear, never premature.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: The customer doesn't care if the supply chain is on time, they care about GE being on time, right?
finding: Redefines delivery and quality metrics from the customer's point of view rather than by internal convention.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: one of our best businesses, lean transformation has real value. It was a year ago that I made my first trip to Evendale, outside of Cincinnati, and met with the lean team. ... I was back there recently, they've reduced it by 1/3 with expectations to cut it again.
finding: Applies lean even in Aviation, the strongest business; he tracks a concrete cash metric (work-to-bill lag cut by a third).

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Part of what we're trying to get at is a level of candor and transparency with the businesses and not always through the formal channels, right? Where we have these operating reviews and these deep dives, and folks can put out, can share tough news, bad news, right?
finding: Builds channels for bad news to surface early from the businesses, and draws his own confidence from that candour.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I would argue that you see a bias here toward retaining the longer-cycle businesses, the better-performing businesses. That core 4 really is, I think, the industrial heart of GE.
finding: Portfolio rule: keep long-cycle, better-performing businesses (Aviation first) and sell others.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We do need to sell off a few more of these businesses so that we've got a balance sheet that would allow us to play offense. ... Again, our priorities there would be Aviation and Healthcare in some form. We're not going to talk names.
finding: Names Aviation (with Healthcare) as the priority for future M&A, conditional on finishing disposals first.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Would have been easy at a time like this to just gut R&D in Renewables, but this is a long-term play.
finding: Keeps funding next-generation product R&D through a cash-negative year rather than cutting it for short-term relief.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: And I'm not a big fan of laying off our performance issues on anybody, be it a supplier, be it a customer or anyone else. It's one thing to be current at these levels. But as the rate goes up, as both intend to do, we need to make sure that we are synchronized with our supply base
finding: Refuses to blame suppliers or customers for LEAP delivery performance and owns supply-base synchronisation.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We are in the midst, clearly, of a platform transition with the narrowbodies. That will create a little bit of margin pressure. But ... we can be in that 20% operating margin range that we've talked about as we work our way through the -- some of the margin headwinds that the LEAP ramp will present for us.
finding: Commits to about 20% Aviation margins through the LEAP ramp; in January 2020 he reports 2019 Aviation margins 'closing above 20%'.
response: Jan 2020: Aviation margins closed above 20% for 2019.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: On track, knock-wood, right? We're looking forward to the first flight this year and service next.
finding: Commits to a 2019 first flight and 2020 entry into service for the GE9X (777X), hedged with 'knock-wood'.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Dennis was here yesterday. I know he said some good things about CFM. We want to make sure, as they ramp, that we're there in lockstep.
finding: Commits CFM to matching Boeing's production ramp, after Boeing's CEO raised LEAP delivery issues.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Right. Well to be clear, we are on schedule at Airbus, have been for some time. We have caught our demands at Boeing. So the challenge from here is really to keep pace as we step up. And we think that's largely on us, right?
finding: Reports LEAP deliveries back on schedule at both airframers and takes ownership of keeping pace as rates rise.
trigger: Analyst raised LEAP delivery delays and castings/forgings supply problems.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: David takes his team up a couple of hours north of here on a regular quarterly basis, where the research group and the Aviation leadership team are talking in great depth over a couple of days as to where technology is going and where the business needs are going.
finding: Holds up Aviation's quarterly technology-business reviews with GE Research as the model for directing R&D to business needs.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: both we and our partners at Safran have talked about our interest and our ongoing dialogue with Boeing in this regard. ... what we want to do is look at the long-term economics for GE. ... But we want to make sure that it is additive to the equation at Aviation.
finding: On the NMA engine he wants CFM (with Safran) in the programme, but only if the long-term economics are additive; he keeps partner and customer talks private.
trigger: Analyst asked under what conditions GE would want to play on Boeing's NMA (a CFM engine).

speaker: Douglas Stuart Harned, Sanford C. Bernstein & Co., LLC., Research Division
quote: Under what conditions would GE want to a play on that? It's a CFM -- it would be a CFM engine. But what would make that attractive or potentially unattractive?
finding: Frames the Boeing NMA engine as a CFM decision; Culp answers that participation depends on additive long-term economics for GE.
response: Culp: interested with Safran, but only if additive to Aviation economics.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: What we said on the industrial side is we want to be at or below 2.5x net debt-to-EBITDA. If you look at where we are today with $55 billion of net debt, that needs to come down dramatically. ... We want to make sure we have a cushion.
finding: Targets 2.5x leverage and wants sources well above the requirement, a cushion-seeking balance-sheet posture.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: And David Joyce made me take a Hippocratic oath when I came on board, right? First, do no harm because it's such a wonderful franchise.
finding: Defers to Aviation's leadership on how the business is run, a light-touch, protect-the-franchise approach to GE's best unit.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I think we really look at that more, frankly, as a function of our own execution as opposed to short cycle pressure that we can point to.
finding: Attributes shortfalls to GE's own execution rather than to the macro environment.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We have not planned for perfection, meaning we have planned conservatively to cover market and execution risks, specifically within our Power business. ... which we now expect to be negative $1 billion to positive $1 billion, while holding our margin guidance.
finding: Raises the FCF guide at mid-year from a deliberately conservative base, a pattern of under-promising then raising.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: And all we're really trying to signal with the $400 million of cash pressure here in the back half -- $400 million per quarter is what is likely to happen if we do not see a return to service. So we just tried to simplify that without getting into trying to get ahead of Boeing or the FAA
finding: Quantifies the MAX cash drag per quarter on a no-return-to-service basis and refuses to guess a return date ahead of Boeing and the FAA.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: At Aviation, we announced record wins at the Paris Air Show, which contributed to sequential backlog growth of 9%. And as it relates to the 737 MAX, we are working closely with Boeing to actively manage production while the fleet remains grounded.
finding: Keeps winning orders while actively throttling LEAP-1B production alongside Boeing during the grounding.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: just in terms of the way the team today is looking at what we call the strike zone in terms of the deals that we want to pursue versus those that we don't, right, we're laying in a global level of standard work. ... They were being sober about cost and contingencies.
finding: Defines a deal 'strike zone' and walks away from bids outside it; contingencies must be priced soberly.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: call it, $3.5 billion of spend over these 3 years, last year, next year in addition to '19, where we typically are going to see a 12- to 24-month payback.
finding: Uses a 12-24 month payback as the hurdle for restructuring spend.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: One, we are not bringing in certain engines in for repair or for overhaul. That's just a function of not have everything we would want to in terms of our own components and the like to service those engines quickly. So I look at that as a supply chain challenge, which we'll work through.
finding: Admits that Aviation services growth is held back by GE's own parts shortages and frames it as a supply-chain problem to fix.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I think as we look forward, again, we hear the call of margin expansion. We'll balance that out with investment, but that will certainly -- that goal will certainly be our bias.
finding: Leans toward Aviation margin expansion over investment while keeping investment in balance.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: If you look at that installed base and that position that we enjoy today at nearly 70,000 engines around the world, that's a function of investing in technology, winning those new platforms and then setting up customer relationships that can span decades, right?
finding: States the engine business model: invest in technology, win platforms, then earn decades of service revenue.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: we want to be optimistic. We want to be positive, but we want to be grounded. ... We know we got caught being a little unduly optimistic in years past. We were slow maybe to tend to the cost structure hoping we'd see a little bit of volume covering that. We're not going to run the business that way.
finding: Will not plan on upside volume even when the market looks better; costs are sized to the base case.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Moving to Slide 3. We're doing what we said we would do.
finding: Signature credibility phrase that points to delivery against stated priorities.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: If and when we do something, we'll have that discussion internally before we have it publicly.
finding: Keeps portfolio options private until decided and does not float strategy in public.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: For Industrial free cash flow, we're raising our full year outlook to breakeven to positive $2 billion.
finding: Raises the FCF guide a second time; the cushion built in March is released stepwise.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Aviation is stronger than expected due to lower allowance and discount payments this year and higher service billings, which has largely offset the year-to-date impact of approximately $1 billion from the 737 MAX grounding.
finding: Offsets about $1bn of MAX cash drag with services and lower airframer allowance payments.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: This quarter, we held sessions with each of our businesses designed to answer 2 fundamental questions: What game are we playing? And how do we win? These were multiday sessions, not flybys, with robust debates about strategy and priorities
finding: Runs deep, multi-day strategy reviews per business around 'what game are we playing, how do we win'.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: you all know early in the life of a new engine program, we're going to see spares represent roughly 10% of sales. We'll see that at the tail end of the program.
finding: Cites the rule that spare engines run at about 10% of programme sales early and late in an engine's life.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: As we think about 2020, I think we're going to try to follow Boeing's lead here when we talk about the full year cash headwinds this year due to MAX that, obviously, assumes that we don't see a return to service this year. That's just, I think, a conservative financial planning assumption
finding: Plans on the pessimistic case (no MAX return in 2019) and follows Boeing's lead on timing.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: At Aviation, we have a strong global franchise with an installed base of nearly 70,000 engines. Service revenues in the quarter were up 7%, and we expanded our win rate on aircraft engine selection to 62% on the A320neo.
finding: Measures CFM's competitive position by its A320neo selection share against Pratt & Whitney's GTF.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I know there was a comment on somebody's call relative to this dynamic that we were going to be building more spare engines. That is indeed not the case, just to make sure we're all on the same page.
finding: Corrects market misinformation about LEAP spare-engine builds directly on the call.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We generated Industrial free cash flow of $3.9 billion in the quarter and $2.3 billion for the full year. This came in ahead of our most recent outlook as Power outperformed expectations and we saw continued strength in Aviation.
finding: Delivers 2019 FCF above all three of his guidance ranges, confirming the conservative-guide, raise-later pattern.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: For the year, margins expanded 60 basis points and 10 basis points organically driven by Power and Healthcare with Aviation margins closing above 20%.
finding: Confirms the 20% Aviation margin commitment was met despite the MAX grounding.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: At Industrial, we reduced net debt by $7 billion, ending the year at a net debt to EBITDA ratio of 4.2x, down from 4.8x a year ago.
finding: Reports deleveraging progress against the 2.5x target, not yet there, with the BioPharma close expected to get there in 2020.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Second is that our plan is dependent on the 737 MAX' return to service, which we are planning for mid-2020, in line with Boeing's commentary. That said, the situation remains fluid.
finding: Ties the 2020 plan to Boeing's mid-2020 return-to-service view rather than his own, and flags uncertainty.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We're expecting organic growth in the low single-digit range for Industrial, organic expansion of up to 75 basis points for Industrial operating margins, $0.50 to $0.60 for adjusted EPS and a range of $2 billion to $4 billion for our Industrial free cash flow.
finding: Issues 2020 guidance with a wide FCF range, the MAX being the main swing factor.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: if you look at Aviation for 2020, again, I think that the outlook there is probably flat to up from a free cash perspective, mindful of all the moving pieces here in and around MAX.
finding: Gives a hedged 2020 Aviation FCF outlook (flat to up) on the MAX assumptions; the outcome is not in this slice.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: In Aviation, the business was able to grow free cash flow versus prior year despite the $1.4 billion of cash headwind from the Boeing 737 MAX grounding.
finding: Absorbs a $1.4bn MAX cash hit while still growing Aviation FCF.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: With respect to corona -- the coronavirus, obviously we're disheartened and sorry that it's happening. It's a tragedy in its own right. Our priority is on safety, clearly, of our team really across GE.
finding: First reaction to COVID (January 2020) is framed around employee safety and Healthcare's role in China; it is not yet seen as an Aviation risk.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: safety first, recertification in concert with the FAA, a safe return to service, delivery of the inventories, and then we'll ramp at a slower, lower rate. Just having that clarity goes a long way to help us best serve Boeing and our airline customers.
finding: Values a clear, sequenced recovery path over speed and accepts a slower, lower LEAP-1B ramp.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We were delivering to Boeing at normal rates through 2019. We're going to see our shipment rates fall roughly half the '19 rate in '20.
finding: Halves LEAP-1B shipments for 2020 after Boeing's production halt, having kept building through 2019.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We need to make sure that we are adjusting our cost structure accordingly but also taking the long view because this will be a temporary wall as Boeing has indicated. And we will be ramping presumably later in the year. So we want to make sure that, not only our teams but our supply chains are prepared to rebound.
finding: Cuts cost for the MAX gap while protecting supply-chain readiness for the rebound; he treats the halt as temporary.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: But we're not bringing that to 0. We very much, if you will, need to keep the lines wet here as we prepare not only for the return to service but the subsequent ramp. ... suppliers like Arconic, PCC and the rest.
finding: Keeps LEAP-1B lines and key suppliers running at reduced rate ('keep the lines wet') rather than stopping, to protect the ramp.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: But a slower pace here will help us not only tend to some delinquencies that we have elsewhere -- past dues that we have elsewhere across Aviation, but I think will also allow us to drive more and better Lean principles into all of our production operations, LEAP and elsewhere.
finding: Uses the forced MAX slowdown to clear past-due deliveries and embed lean in LEAP production.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We'll deal with MAX as it comes. But long term, clearly, this is going to be our strongest cash-generating business across the portfolio.
finding: Treats MAX as transitory and Aviation as GE's long-term cash engine.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: But going forward, I think we have real conviction in the LEAP engine. Clearly, Boeing is 1 of 2 major customers for that engine. And I think going forward, that should be a very healthy relationship and a very strong program for us.
finding: Keeps long-term conviction in LEAP and in Boeing as one of its two anchor customers despite the crisis.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: just a heightened level of discipline upfront when we're talking about new business, ... not only in terms of price but frankly terms, conditions, scope, everything that can go into making a new order, be it for equipment or service, positive and accretive or not.
finding: Demands that every new order be accretive on price, terms and scope; underwriting discipline over volume.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Andrew, as you know well, we have an excellent relationship with Airbus. I was with them just last week, in fact. ... But I think on balance, we have work to do with our friends at Airbus, work we're committed to.
finding: Handles Airbus's push on engine-supplier payables diplomatically; he calls Airbus a close partner, admits 'work to do' and avoids public friction.
trigger: Analyst asked about Airbus's 2020 payables adjustments affecting engine suppliers.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Clearly, he'll put safety first. Real respect for the primacy of the FAA. Pulling the end on as they did to stop the line takes a lot of guts. I respect that.
finding: Publicly backs Boeing's new CEO and the decision to stop the MAX line, a supportive stance toward the airframer customer.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I think GECAS is a business that is certainly a good, strong business, helps us just in general, certainly has ties to GE Aviation. How that plays out over time, again, I think we have optionality once we are deleveraged and the businesses are performing well.
finding: Leaves GECAS's future open and ties any portfolio move to finishing deleveraging first.
trigger: Analyst asked about the future of GE Capital.
response: March 2021: combined GECAS with AerCap for over $30B, keeping a 46% stake.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Is it time to play offense yet? It's getting closer, right? ... We need to work through some of these near-term challenges in and around the 737 MAX. I think as we do that, and the denominator is fortified as well, we're going to be able to play offense. ... At times, you might think we're being a little conservative.
finding: Ties any move to offense to fixing EBITDA, including clearing the 737 MAX issues, and accepts being seen as conservative.
trigger: Analyst asked about capital deployment after the BioPharma proceeds.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: So with the passage of a little bit of time, I think we have the balance sheet that gives us flexibility and optionality, and we should have the businesses in place where if other structures, other arrangements make sense, you'll see us do that. But no business has a holiday here from improved performance.
finding: Keeps structural options open once the balance sheet is ready but demands improvement from every business in the meantime.
trigger: Analyst asked about strategic options after deleveraging.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: So I think when you look at restructuring 2019, you really need to put it in the context of the $2.5 billion that we spent the last couple of years, investments which we think basically have a 12- to 24-month payback. They're very much in line with what I have seen and done elsewhere.
finding: Uses a 12-24 month payback benchmark for restructuring spending.
trigger: Analyst asked why 2019 restructuring spend was below plan.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: And as we look at the future of GE Aviation, I think we feel very confident that, that $4-plus billion cash flow level, once we get through some of the near-term challenges with MAX, is going to continue to grow and be sustainable.
finding: Commits to Aviation sustaining and growing $4B+ of annual free cash flow once the MAX is resolved.
response: COVID hit weeks later; in February 2021 he again expressed confidence in returning to 2019's $4B+.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: But given what we know at this point, I think we'll be on our way in the back half with respect to the return to service given everything that we've heard from Boeing and elsewhere. And that'll be good for us.
finding: Forecasts a second-half 2020 return to service for the MAX, based on Boeing's guidance.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: all we were really saying was that a business like GE with this portfolio yielding 4%, 5% free cash should be able to double that. We didn't put a timetable on that. ... In turn, we delivered the $2.3 billion of free cash that we did.
finding: Explains the long-term cash goal as a doubling with no date, and points to 2019's $2.3B as delivery against conservative planning.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Corona, certainly a bit of a wild card for us, like everybody. So I think we're going to see here in the first quarter free cash probably in the range of a negative $2 billion, right? So we'll be about $800 million off largely due to MAX.
finding: Quantifies the 737 MAX grounding hit to cash ahead of time and flags COVID only as a wild card in February 2020.
trigger: 737 MAX grounding; early COVID in China.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: It'll just be an operating challenge here in the first half given that we will have a temporary slowdown, but we don't want to take out too much of our cost structure given the snapback that we know is inevitable here in the back half and in the years to come.
finding: During the MAX grounding, chose to keep LEAP-1B capacity and cost in place for the expected rebound rather than cut deeply.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: It's easy to say let's focus on cash. It's easy to say let's change our incentive comp system and put more emphasis on free cash flow. But it would be like asking me or paying me to dunk a basketball, I still couldn't do it.
finding: Believes in changing processes over changing incentives: pay alone does not build capability.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I'm on the road, I think, virtually every week in the businesses with customers, in the labs, in the factories, trying to make sure that my information flow is not just through formal channels but complemented by those things I should pick up along the way.
finding: Collects first-hand information in factories and with customers to check what formal reporting tells him.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: That, in many respects, is job 1 at GE: continuing to nurture and grow the Aviation franchise. ... we have a strong leadership position and a global growth market with a really nice balance between multiple OE platforms
finding: Names growing the Aviation franchise as GE's first job, based on a mix of several OE platforms and a long-term service backlog.
trigger: Analyst cited bearish views on the aerospace cycle.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: And Aviation at 20%, Renewables with a negative number, everybody has margin expansion potential. If you don't think so, you'll never realize it, right? ... It might be a little harder in Aviation given where they start, but when you sit with David Joyce and the team, plenty of opportunities to continue to accrete margins and drive better cash performance.
finding: Pushes for margin expansion even in GE's best business (Aviation at ~20%), on the view that expectations come first.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: It's just the nature of the work, as you well know, it carries with it risk. You want to make sure you are paid for taking that risk, and you're doing all you can to mitigate.
finding: Takes on project risk only if it is priced in and mitigated.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: And we don't take any of that for granted, right? We've got to compete for every new engine platform order. We have to compete for every next shop visit. We can always improve how we run the business, be it from a cost or from a cash perspective.
finding: Sees no entitlement in incumbency: GE must win every new engine platform and every next shop visit.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I think Carolina coming in is going to bring a different skill set, a different perspective coming from the outside. Carolina and I, in many respects, grew up in parallel universes, right, in companies that had more of a decentralized approach to life, very much cash-oriented, lean, all of that.
finding: Chose an outside CFO who shares his decentralised, cash-focused, lean philosophy, so the CEO and CFO are closely aligned.
trigger: CFO transition from Jamie Miller to Carolina Dybeck Happe.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: part of the cultural journey that we're on at GE is very much geared toward making sure that bad news travels fast, if you will. ... make sure that they're telling me or they're telling their boss what they think as opposed to what they think their boss might want to hear.
finding: Builds a culture where bad news travels fast and people say what they think rather than what the boss wants to hear.
trigger: Analyst asked how he knows he is getting accurate information.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: the conviction is very high in that high single-digit cash yield number over the long term. So I think, quite deliberately, we didn't try to circle this year or that year with that in mind. ... we need to demonstrate that we can do this over time in a sustained way.
finding: Gives no date for long-term targets until the progress supports one.
trigger: Analyst asked when GE would reach high single-digit cash yield.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: we ended 2019 with Industrial leverage of 4.2x net debt to EBITDA, down from 4.8x at the end of 2018. We continue to target achieving our Industrial leverage goal of less than 2.5x net debt to EBITDA in 2020.
finding: Commits to a dated leverage target (<2.5x in 2020) on a measurable path.
response: May 2020: target kept but timing pushed out because of COVID.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Our 2020 target is a range of a positive $2 billion to $4 billion. And from there, higher in '21 and '22. In aggregate, over the long term, we expect that our Industrial businesses should yield high single-digit free cash flow margins.
finding: Sets a wide 2020 cash range and a long-term high single-digit free cash flow margin aim; it excluded COVID beyond Q1.
response: Guidance withdrawn within weeks as COVID spread; actual 2020 FCF was $0.6B.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: And working capital should be a significant positive in 2020, primarily driven by the 737 MAX agreement with Boeing that David outlined, which should result in the collection of outstanding AR balances.
finding: Settles the cash impact of the 737 MAX grounding through an agreement with Boeing, to collect overdue receivables in 2020.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: and I'm not going to sugarcoat this, we got hit hard in some of our highest-margin parts of our best-performing businesses. This is especially true at Aviation services, where COVID-19 caused a rapid decline in commercial aviation demand
finding: Delivers bad news directly and names Aviation services, GE's best profit pool, as the hardest hit.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: So we're redefining winning from margin expansion in 2020 to improving our decremental margins this year, which requires we aggressively adjust our cost structure. That's what winning looks like for Aviation ... To be clear, we'll get back to targeting those 20% operating margins post pandemic.
finding: Swaps the 2020 Aviation goal from margin growth to limiting decrementals while committing to return to 20% operating margins after the pandemic.
response: June 2021: still targets high-teens to 20% margins as volumes recover.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I think that we took guidance off the table a few weeks back and didn't want to take an attempt at framing formal guidance here today. ... that's what we know, and that's what we're comfortable sharing.
finding: Withdrew the March 2020 guidance within weeks and gave data, not a forecast, until visibility returned.
response: Withdrawal of the 4 March 2020 outlook ($2-4B FCF).

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We've previously announced $500 million to $1 billion in cost and cash actions, and we've now increased this, targeting more than $1 billion in cost actions and more than $2 billion in cash actions. ... These include a 10% reduction in Aviation's total U.S. workforce and furloughs impacting 50% of its U.S. maintenance repair and overhaul facilities and new engine manufacturing.
finding: Escalates Aviation cost and cash actions within weeks, using layoffs and broad furloughs across both repair shops and new-engine plants.
trigger: Departures down ~75%; 60% of the CFM fleet parked.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: That said, we're preparing for elevated repossessions and redeployments as well as lease restructurings, and we've had approximately 80% of our customers seek short-term deferrals. As you may have seen, we've agreed with Boeing on a rebalancing of our 737 MAX order book.
finding: Through GECAS, prepares for lessee distress and renegotiates its own 737 MAX order book with Boeing.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: in terms of the temporary lack of works, that was a way to quickly adjust our cost structure in that business on a variable basis to these shockingly fast changes in demand. ... We need to work through the changes on a more permanent basis that are required in light of the length of the recovery that we're looking at.
finding: Uses fast temporary measures first and then converts them into permanent restructuring once the length of the downturn is clear.
trigger: Analyst asked how much of the cost action was permanent.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I'm not sure we would buy into the premise per se, right? I mean we are a cycles business much more so than any other indicator. And those cycles are going to have to come back before the passengers do.
finding: Rejects an analyst's framing and uses engine cycles (departures), not passengers, as the driver of aftermarket decisions.
trigger: Analyst's premise about the aftermarket recovery path.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Here, I draw on my experience as a CEO managing through 9/11 and the global financial crisis. There are 3 steps in this model: embrace reality, redefine winning and execute the plan. Easy to say, hard to do.
finding: Applies a crisis playbook from earlier downturns he led as a CEO: embrace reality, redefine winning, execute the plan.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We're going to acknowledge that uncertainty, hence the pulling of the guide, but we're not going to sit back and hope that it all passes. We're not going to take the view that we've got a sharp rebound coming ... We're going to do everything we possibly can to control our destiny here without impairing the long-term value
finding: Acts early on costs instead of waiting for a rebound, while guarding long-term value.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: in the second quarter, we see installed engines down roughly 45% and spare engines down roughly 60% year-on-year, attributable to the delivery deferrals in addition to the already planned lower production rate on the 737 MAX. In the near term, we're rightsizing production capacity and actively managing the supply base.
finding: Responds to the collapse in engine deliveries, on top of the planned lower MAX rate, by rightsizing production and managing suppliers closely.
trigger: Airframer delivery deferrals plus the 737 MAX rate cut.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We came into this year knowing we were going to have to adjust to a different schedule with the MAX, chasing the step-up at Airbus with the 320neo while dealing with a good bit of past due on the commercial side, both OE and aftermarket, while having pretty good military demand to contend with.
finding: Describes the pre-COVID LEAP supply problem: MAX schedule changes, chasing the A320neo ramp and late deliveries in both new engines and spares.
trigger: Analyst asked about working capital in Aviation.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: So after a period of time, as the aftermarket has grown as it has the last decade, this is going to give us an opportunity to rethink, to consolidate all the while mindful of our obligations to customers ... to make sure that we have a lean cost structure with adequate capacity to come out of the downturn here
finding: Uses the downturn to consolidate the service shop footprint built during a decade of growth, but keeps enough capacity for the recovery.
trigger: Analyst asked about restructuring the Aviation aftermarket business.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: we were ramping spares with both the LEAP-1A and the LEAP-1B as the narrow-body market was taking off, typical early in the life of an engine activity. We are clearly seeing that soften, not necessarily going to 0, as preparations are being made for the return to service of the MAX, right? I don't think that opportunity is lost.
finding: Treats the LEAP spare-engine ramp as deferred, not lost: it slides out a few years with the MAX return and the slower recovery.
trigger: Analyst asked about the drop in spare-engine shipments.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: as we went through the mechanics of the future billings, the future costs related to those billings, based on the information at the time, it was really just $100 billion -- $100 million adjustment, noncash of course ... these are 10- to 15-year agreements as you know, and those adjustments are taken in the context of that particularly extended time period.
finding: Treats service contract charges in the context of 10-15 year contract lives, so a short-term utilisation shock is marked but not over-reacted to.
trigger: Analyst asked about risk in the $234B Aviation service backlog.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Well, we -- it did come at a good time. There's no question. That's why we put the emphasis in the BioPharma setup on certainty, right? We want to take the market risk off the table relative to thinking through the Healthcare options.
finding: Designed the BioPharma sale for certainty to remove market risk, putting secure liquidity ahead of maximum value.
trigger: Analyst noted the $20B BioPharma proceeds arrived just as COVID hit.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Additionally, roughly 62% of our GE/CFM fleet has seen one shop visit or less, and this will generate demand upon recovery. We have more narrow-bodies that are 10 years or younger than the narrow-body installed base of the rest of the industry.
finding: Claims a structural aftermarket edge over rival engine makers: a younger narrowbody fleet than the rest of the industry combined.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: As you'll see on the right, we have strong positions, sole source on 2 of the biggest new engine entrants and a 65% win rate on the other. While we acknowledge there's pressure on near-term demand for new aircraft, these stats demonstrate that customers see the value of GE technology.
finding: Cites sole-source positions on two big new platforms and a 65% win rate on the contested one (presumably the A320neo, where LEAP competes with Pratt & Whitney's GTF) as proof of competitive strength.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Last year, our Aviation business saw a total of $1.8 billion of R&D spending, which includes our own dollars and funding from customers and partners. Half of that came from partners and customers, a majority of which was funded by the U.S. government and directed to that military systems business.
finding: Shows that half of Aviation R&D is funded by others (mostly the U.S. government for military), which cuts GE's own development risk.
trigger: Shareholder asked how much of GE's spending is military.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I'm smiling, and that's the sad reality of doing this by way of a conference call rather than in person. But frankly, our current debt loads reflect historic borrowing that became too large relative to the earnings potential of the company over time.
finding: Speaks candidly about past over-borrowing instead of defending legacy decisions.
trigger: Shareholder asked why GE had so much debt.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Well, as I indicated, we're probably not going to be hyperactive on the business development front anytime soon. And I would rarely -- well, I think I've made a practice never to speak prospectively about M&A.
finding: Never comments on M&A in advance and signals little appetite for deals while deleveraging.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Rest assured, we remain committed to achieving our deleveraging goal of less than 2.5x industrial net debt-to-EBITDA in industrial and less than 4x debt-to-equity in capital. We remain committed to our deleveraging targets, but expect it will take a longer period of time than previously announced due to the uncertainty associated with COVID 19.
finding: Keeps the leverage ceilings but openly moves the date back, resetting the timetable rather than dropping the targets.
response: Resets the March 2020 plan to reach <2.5x in 2020.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: When we announced these actions in late March, I announced that I would forgo my salary in its entirety for the rest of the year, starting on April 1. In addition, David Joyce, the Head of our Aviation business, has forgone half of his salary.
finding: Pairs the COVID layoffs with visible pay sacrifice by himself and the Aviation CEO, showing leaders sharing the pain.
trigger: Shareholder asked what pay changes management took while employees were furloughed.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: the first and most important step to make sure that we come out a better, stronger GE on the other side of this pandemic is to embrace our reality. ... Difficult but foundational because we know that undue optimism won't serve us particularly well today.
finding: Makes facing the downside the first crisis step and explicitly rejects optimism as a basis for planning.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I think that the first 777X has had now 30 successful test flights. The engines have performed very well. ... I believe that we are ready to go with our partner, Boeing, on a second plane. The engines are ready to go there as well.
finding: Reports progress on the GE9X / 777X flight tests and calls Boeing a partner, putting the engine on schedule ahead of the airframe.
trigger: Shareholder asked about GE9X engine hours on the 777X.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: It's difficult to predict when air travel fully will resume, but the reality is it will not be soon. So we're adjusting our cost structure to ensure Aviation will remain well positioned when the industry recovers. And when it does, we'll be there with the largest and youngest installed base of all engine manufacturers.
finding: Claims the largest and youngest installed base of any engine maker, an edge over Pratt & Whitney and Rolls-Royce, and resizes costs to protect that position.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: we were coming into this moment, Doug, anyway, having refreshed, again, both the narrowbody and the widebody platforms, recognizing that we could take a little bit of gas off the engineering engine. So I think this year, you're going to see us probably spend, call it, several hundred million dollars less in engineering overall as we adjust to this environment.
finding: Cuts Aviation engineering spend because the LEAP and GE9X programmes are done and no new airplane is in sight; R&D follows the airframe launch cycle.
trigger: Analyst noted the NMA had been shelved and no new airplane was on the horizon.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: From a capital perspective, we're probably going to be down at this rate, call it, 25%, just, again, in light of the cash pressures, the overall reductions in volume in the business. If we can cut a little bit more, we will do that.
finding: Cuts Aviation capex by about a quarter in the downturn and will cut further if possible.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: if different arrangements, different structures are going to serve the businesses well over time, I think we're going to be open to that. ... So I don't think we're going to be necessarily wed to any one philosophy other than starting each day with the businesses and making the businesses stronger our overarching objective.
finding: Is not attached to the conglomerate model; open to other structures once the balance sheet is fixed, with business strength as the test.
trigger: Analyst asked about the market's discount on multi-industry companies.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I think we're looking in the second quarter at a mark there on the CSA book probably in the hundreds of millions of dollars. We had a modest write-down in the first quarter. You're going to see again a bigger number here in the second quarter given what we know today.
finding: Pre-announces a larger charge on the long-term service contract book a quarter ahead instead of letting it surprise investors.
trigger: Lower utilisation hurting service contract (CSA) margins.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Doug, I really think it is a delay rather than a redirection. But that said, I think one reason we took guidance down back in April at earnings is that the near-term visibility that we have and what it implies for the medium and long term just isn't there for us to put that stake in the ground.
finding: Withdrew guidance rather than issue numbers he could not support, while keeping the long-term thesis.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We, at this point, think in the second quarter, we're going to see our free cash flow number come in at a negative level, probably in the $3.5 billion to $4.5 billion band as best we can tell today. ... But I think 2020 is likely to be a negative free cash flow year for GE
finding: Gives a deliberately bleak cash forecast during the crisis.
response: 2Q came in at -$2.1B (above guide); full-year 2020 was +$0.6B.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Nearly 1/4 of the workforce being reduced, unfortunately. But again, in the spirit of embracing our reality, that's what we're doing. And one of the ways where we're redefining winning in this business is to improve the 62% decremental margin that we saw in the first quarter.
finding: Cuts about a quarter of Aviation's workforce and resets the Aviation scorecard from margin growth to limiting decremental margins.
trigger: COVID collapse in departures and shop visits.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: In addition to COVID, as we talked about, right, everything with respect to the MAX was something that we were not anticipating, tragedies, and that continues to be something we're working through with our friends at Boeing.
finding: Names the 737 MAX grounding as the main outside surprise of his tenure besides COVID and frames it as ongoing joint work with Boeing.
trigger: Analyst asked what had surprised him most since becoming CEO.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: $2 billion of cost reductions, $3 billion of cash preservation actions. Doug, I think 1/3 to 1/2 of that will be permanent in nature if we just close the ... books on it today. We clearly want to push more of that to be permanent given that we know, particularly with Aviation, we're going to have a multiyear challenge here
finding: Sizes the COVID response at $2B cost and $3B cash and tries to make more of it permanent because Aviation faces a multi-year downturn.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: part of the planning is done, if you will, with an axe more directional in nature. Other parts of it, if you will, are more precise, perhaps with the scalpel. ... we need to take dramatic action on the cost side to deal with that
finding: Uses a two-speed approach in the crisis: fast, broad cuts first, then precise adjustments as airline fleet decisions become clear.
trigger: Analyst asked how Aviation plans capacity with aftermarket pressure likely to persist.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We really want to protect the underlying future technology bets that have always defined GE Aviation and driven our industry leadership. That's still important. None of us know exactly how the future is going to play out, but there will be a need for new technologies, next-gen engine platforms. We want to make sure that we're there.
finding: Ring-fences long-term next-generation engine technology even while cutting near-term engineering, to be ready for the next platform whenever it comes.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I don't think that the sequential improvement that we see in the second half is going to take us into a zone that starts with a 3, but I think we will be in a zone with a 4, with the third quarter showing us some modest improvement.
finding: Gives a specific, modest 2H20 target for Aviation decremental margins (the 40s) and declines the analyst's more optimistic 30s.
trigger: Analyst noted Aviation decrementals of 48% excluding charges and asked if they could reach 30-40%.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: And Industrial free cash flow came in above the guide we provided in May at a negative $2.1 billion, better, but obviously still negative.
finding: Beats his own May forecast (negative $3.5-4.5B) by a wide margin, which fits a conservative guiding style.
response: Outcome of the 28 May 2020 2Q cash forecast.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We think we're well positioned to participate given that USM is a source of material for our CSAs. It has been for many years. ... Again, I don't think we're looking for anyone to do us any favors. I don't think we have a different posture than anyone else in the industry.
finding: Expects to use retirements and used material to feed its service contracts, and claims no special protection from customers or the industry.
trigger: Analyst asked about retirements and used serviceable material.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We're planning for a steep market decline this year and likely a slow multiyear recovery. Long term though, the aviation market has solid fundamentals, and we're committed to protecting the future of this business and our leadership position within the industry.
finding: Plans for a slow multi-year recovery yet commits to protecting Aviation's long-term position: cut deep for the short term, protect the long term.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: It was not easy to find a worthy successor to David, but I'm very excited to welcome John Slattery, a proven leader with extensive global commercial aviation experience to our team.
finding: Hires an outside leader with commercial aviation experience to succeed long-time GE Aviation CEO David Joyce in the middle of the crisis.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I think you've seen us try to avoid saying we're going to be back at this date or that date for certain. ... this industry will recover. There's no doubt in my mind about that. It's really a function of time. ... It's not going to be next year.
finding: Refuses to name a recovery date yet is certain of recovery, and rules out a 2021 return.
trigger: Analyst asked how close the industry was to a recovery.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I've been impressed as a relative newcomer how, even at these critical junctures, the industry is so hyper-focused on safety, right? And some of that comes in the wake of what happened with the 737 MAX.
finding: Links the industry's COVID return-to-flight safety stance to lessons from the 737 MAX, which he supports as a supplier.
trigger: Analyst asked what GE had learned from customers during COVID.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Various customers have varying degrees of balance sheet strength. Everyone's trying to work through that smartly, not only with lenders but also with suppliers like us. We see that, obviously, both on the OE ... side and on the aftermarket side of the business. ... We're certainly getting impacted in our biggest, most profitable business.
finding: Acknowledges customer credit risk on both engine sales and services, with suppliers like GE asked to help weaker airlines.
trigger: Analyst asked about customer conversations during COVID.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We don't want to ever be in a position where we're under-investing in innovation, dare I say safety or quality. ... one of the benefits we'll get from a true lean transformation at GE is we'll just have, I think, a sharper, more critical eye with respect to how we think about capital more broadly
finding: Protects innovation, safety and quality spending but expects lean to shrink capex needs.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: From day 1, we've known this would be a game of inches. This is still true today.
finding: Signature framing: the turnaround is a series of small gains, not one big fix.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Joe, I appreciate that feedback on my MO. We're just trying to build and improve here at GE. ... we think at least $2.5 billion is the right outlook at this point, given what we know and don't.
finding: Accepts an analyst's description of him as setting conservative goalposts and keeps the floor-style guide unchanged.
trigger: Analyst: 'your MO historically has been to be conservative when you set goalposts like this.'

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: we expect fourth quarter Industrial free cash flow of at least $2.5 billion, with positive contributions from all segments, but how much more really depends on how aviation fares through the quarter. And importantly, the momentum we're building should help us deliver positive industrial free cash flow in 2021.
finding: Sets a floor ('at least') rather than a point estimate and names Aviation as the swing factor.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: On Slide 4, you'll see GE CFM departures, which drives our service business much more so than RPKs. As a reminder, we track departures by region and by platform daily.
finding: Runs the aviation business on a daily, platform-level departures dashboard and treats departures, not RPKs, as the driver of service revenue.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Services are critical to the recovery of Aviation as we generate much of our cash here, especially within narrowbodies, which are more than 40% of our historical revenue. We typically have good line of sight into demand of about 6 weeks out at our internal jobs, but we have less visibility into external shop visits.
finding: Puts narrowbody services (CFM56/LEAP) at the core of Aviation cash and is open about how short its demand visibility is.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Shipments out of the airframers triggers our AD&A obligations, a working capital dynamic there that could go against us. And I think we've shared before that we have past due, particularly on our military business. We're not happy with that.
finding: Flags airframer delivery timing as a cash risk through the allowances and concessions paid to airframers (AD&A) tied to engine shipments, and owns the military delinquencies plainly.
trigger: Analyst asked how much of the 4Q20 cash target was within GE's control.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We made an important organizational move in aviation services with Russell Stokes returning to Aviation as CEO of that business. Russell will lead our aviation services business in a new role, integrating both our commercial and operations team.
finding: Restructures Aviation services under one leader who owns both commercial and repair operations, to tie pricing and shop work together.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I don't think any of our businesses are close to optimizing their underlying performance. ... And over time, we're going to be open to ways to deliver value, maximize value at GE.
finding: Fixes business performance before portfolio moves but keeps structural options open.
trigger: Analyst asked about portfolio evolution given high market valuations.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I think what we try to do here is provide a framework that isn't assuming some sort of out-of-consensus early spike recovery in Aviation. That would be, in a word, foolish.
finding: Builds guidance on a conservative, consensus-or-below Aviation recovery and openly rejects betting on an early rebound.
trigger: Analyst asked what drives the width of the 2021 cash range.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Industrial free cash flow came in at $4.4 billion in the quarter, $0.5 billion higher than last year. ... For the year, we generated positive free cash flow of $600 million or $300 million excluding BioPharma in the first quarter.
finding: Beat his own October guide of at least $2.5B for 4Q20 and turned 2020 cash positive after forecasting a negative year in May.
response: Outcome of the October 2020 '$2.5B or more' guide and the May 2020 'negative year' call.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We're expecting organic growth in the low single-digit range for Industrial revenue, organic expansion of 250-plus basis points for Industrial operating margin, $0.15 to $0.25 for adjusted EPS and a range of $2.5 billion to $4.5 billion for Industrial free cash flow.
finding: Restores formal annual guidance with wide ranges after pulling it in 2020.
response: Kept unchanged at the March 2021 outlook and the April 2021 Q1 call.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Clearly, our supply chain has been through a roller coaster right there along with us. I mean it was a year ago -- I mean, literally, right now, when we're talking about not only continued volume ramps, but a new introduction clearly at Boeing with the MAX and then literally weeks later we're talking about slamming on the brakes.
finding: Describes the whiplash from planning MAX and LEAP ramps to an abrupt stop, and frames supplier support through the swing as part of the job.
trigger: COVID collapse in early 2020, just as the MAX return and LEAP ramp were being planned.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: At GE Aviation, we continue to expect the engine aftermarket recovery to lag departure trends across regions and fleets, particularly around quarantine requirements. And given that we generate a significant portion of our cash in Commercial Services, the recovery of the aftermarket remains critical.
finding: Puts the commercial engine aftermarket at the centre of the plan as Aviation's cash engine, and builds in a lag behind departures.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I think people need to appreciate that USM cuts both ways for us. We're -- we've been a major user of USM given the nature of our CSA obligations over time. ... from our perspective, we anticipate deliveries to outpace retirements and that will be a net effect positive for us at Aviation.
finding: Sees used serviceable material as both a threat to spare-parts sales and a cost lever for its long-term service contracts; net, expects new deliveries to outpace retirements.
trigger: Analyst asked about aircraft retirements and used serviceable material.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: we've got a little over half of the CFM56-5B and -7B fleet, they haven't seen their first shop visit, right? ... 3/4 of that same fleet have yet to see their second shop visit. ... Our major economics happen in and around the first and second.
finding: Pins CFM56 aftermarket profit on the first and second shop visits and argues the young -5B/-7B fleet still has most of them ahead.
trigger: Analyst asked about retirements and used material in the recovery.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We didn't bring that activity level down to 0. We tried to resize it in a way that embraced this harsh, unfortunate near-term reality, but gave us a little bit of room ... we'll leverage some of the, if you will, the excess cost that is still there because again, we didn't take it to the bone.
finding: Deliberately kept spare service capacity in the COVID cuts, accepting some excess cost now to be able to serve the rebound.
trigger: Analyst asked how far Aviation services capacity had been cut ahead of a recovery.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Julian, I think we have a lot of confidence we can get back to 2019 levels, as you say, over $4 billion in free cash in Aviation. ... With the refresh of our product lineup, there's no reason that, that can't continue to be true.
finding: Commits to restoring Aviation free cash flow to 2019 levels (over $4B), relying on the young fleet and the renewed product line.
response: Restates the February 2020 view that Aviation's $4B+ cash level is sustainable, now after COVID.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: given what we've been focused on relative to the deleveraging and improving the operational foundation, I was very keen to make sure that we didn't undermine those efforts, thinking about, if you will, the -- often the more enjoyable parts of the job in terms of getting out, driving innovation, spending time with customers
finding: Deliberately delayed growth and innovation talk until the balance sheet and operations were fixed: one thing at a time.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: every new platform that GE has ever come forward with, be it narrow bodies, be it wide bodies, has been largely about energy efficiency. That won't change as we think about the future of flight and everything the industry has pledged to do by 2050.
finding: Holds fuel efficiency as the constant design driver for every new engine platform and ties the future product roadmap to the industry's 2050 pledge.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: our Industrial cash needs probably are, call it, $13 billion or less. So we know we're in a position today where we've got additional liquidity. ... So we've, as you well know, taken a rather conservative posture relative to the balance sheet during the pandemic.
finding: Holds excess liquidity above a stated ~$13B operating need through the pandemic, putting balance sheet safety ahead of using the cash.
trigger: Analyst asked about using excess cash.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I know a number of people inside the company, at least, think that when we say playing offense, we're going to go do a lot of lateral, big M&A. That's not the agenda, right. Organic first, and then we'll do some bolt-ons when we can, where it makes sense.
finding: Rules out big transformational M&A; growth is organic first, with small bolt-ons only.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: when you have a portfolio of different businesses as we do at GE, management and the Board need to constantly evaluate the role of every business in the portfolio, right. No business necessarily has a permanent home. We all have to earn our keep
finding: Treats the portfolio as always under review; no business is permanent, which leaves room for break-ups and exits.
trigger: Analyst asked whether businesses that miss the cash goals should stay in GE.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Aviation is the service business that matters most. ... We've got a new leader in our services portfolio, Russell Stokes. A lot of change going on there to make sure we have a cost structure for today and capacity for tomorrow
finding: Ranks Aviation services first among GE's service businesses and installs a new leader to cut cost now while keeping shop capacity for the rebound.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: A lot of what we're trying to do is not muscle a supplier or hold our breath at quarter end but really lay in the process, be it in the new-build side, be it in services, to make sure we have real pull systems, driven first and foremost by on-time delivery targets.
finding: Manages the supply chain through pull systems and on-time delivery targets rather than squeezing suppliers or end-of-quarter pushes.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: sets us on an accelerated path toward being a far better capitalized company, which then, in turn, will allow us to play offense from a capital allocation perspective. That's still, I think, a couple of years down the road, though. ... we've got a balance sheet where we can really entertain those questions as practical ones rather than as theoretical considerations.
finding: Sequences capital deployment strictly: deleverage first, with M&A and offense 'a couple of years' out.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: for a transaction like this to come together, you really need 3 dynamics ... One, we needed to be in a position where we had a strong enough foundation to consider a move like this. ... if we were lacking any one of those 3 considerations, we wouldn't have this introduction to our outlook call today.
finding: States an explicit three-part gate for big portfolio moves (a strong enough foundation, the right partner, supportive markets) and will not act unless all three are met.
trigger: Analyst asked why the GECAS-AerCap deal was happening now.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: And as the industry recovers, that equity stake that we have in the combined business, undoubtedly, will be worth more than it is today. We would have never sold GECAS for cash at this point in the cycle. Fortunately, that's really not what we're doing today.
finding: Refuses to sell an aviation asset for cash at the bottom of the cycle; structures the exit with a 46% equity stake to keep the upside from the recovery.
trigger: Combining GECAS with AerCap in March 2021, during the COVID trough.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: This includes corporate, which looks much different today with a focus on strategy, capital allocation, research, talent and governance. To this end, we've transferred certain shared service responsibilities and related third-party contracts back into the businesses. This empowers our businesses to control these costs.
finding: Keeps only strategy, capital allocation, research, talent and governance at corporate and pushes operating decisions and costs down to the businesses.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I'm not sure I would buy into your premise that we've got the visibility that you're suggesting that we do. ... So I think what we're going to do going forward is what we've done here in the last several years, tell you what we know, tell you what we don't.
finding: Pushes back when analysts read in more certainty than he has; his stated guidance rule is to say what is known and what is not.
trigger: Analyst suggested GE had good visibility to raise the 2021 guide.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: there's no question that we feel confident today about our potential to deliver on that high single-digit free cash flow margin in '23 or hopefully shortly thereafter, right? ... So there's no declaration of victory here.
finding: Now puts a date (2023 or shortly after) on the high single-digit free cash flow margin goal, having declined to name a year in March 2020.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: At Aviation, CFM secured LEAP engine and service agreements from Southwest Airlines and Scandinavian Airlines to power 100 MAX and 35 A320neo aircraft.
finding: Highlights CFM wins that bundle LEAP engines with service agreements on both the MAX and the A320neo, as signs of recovery.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We've got less visibility on the channel side of things. And I think we clearly see signs that over the last several quarters, a number of our partners have brought inventory levels down. ... But like any distribution or third-party-related business I've ever seen, you see those behaviors in the downturn and then you get a lift off that base.
finding: Reads the aftermarket through a distributor-destocking lens and expects a restocking lift in the recovery, while admitting limited visibility into third-party shops.
trigger: Analyst asked about the value per shop visit and the spare-parts channel.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: when we talk about selectivity, that really is about price and margins, but also about terms and conditions, which I think of as really, if you will, risk that isn't necessarily modeled, but can come back and course through and wreck the P&L if we're not careful.
finding: Underwrites deals on contract terms as well as price, treating unmodelled contract risk as a reason to walk away.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I think I go back in my Lean training, right, SQDC safety, quality, delivery, cost in that order. It's not an acronym. It's a priority set.
finding: States a fixed ranking for trade-offs: safety, then quality, then delivery, then cost.
trigger: Shareholder asked for the most important metric on his dashboard.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Aviation improved margins through the year and delivered nearly breakeven free cash flow. Our GE9X engine was certified by the U.S. FAA, completing our commercial product portfolio renewal with groundbreaking efficiency gains in every market.
finding: Presents the engine line-up as fully renewed (LEAP, GE9X) and points to cash discipline in Aviation through the 2020 downturn.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We want to get back to a more competitive dividend, right? It's been a while, buybacks ought to be part of that conversation, let alone redeployment back into the business. Admittedly, we haven't spent a ton of time on that given the deleveraging in the operational transformation.
finding: Signals that dividends and buybacks come back only after deleveraging and the operational fix are done.
trigger: Audience asked about capital allocation once the $7B cash target is reached.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: A lot of investors will ask, "Well, why not raise it?" Well, I appreciate the confidence born of that question, but we're not going to raise it until we do it.
finding: Will not raise a long-term target until it has been delivered: under-promise, then prove it.
trigger: Investors asking whether to raise the high single-digit free cash flow margin aspiration.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Our views relative to recovery don't change here. We think narrowbodies are back in '23, widebodies in '24. I think that's more or less a consensus view. What we want to do is make sure we're ready for the snapback
finding: Gives a dated, consensus-anchored recovery call (narrowbodies 2023, widebodies 2024) and frames the job as being ready for the snapback rather than calling it early.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: cost out on our book, right, $1 billion last year, $500 million this year. Some of that's going to come back, no question ... And that's why I think we have the confidence we can get back to that high-teens 20% op margin level as volumes recover in Aviation.
finding: Commits to restoring Aviation margins to the high teens / 20% as volumes return, while admitting part of the COVID cost-out will come back.
response: Reaffirms the April 2020 pledge to return to 20% Aviation margins after the pandemic.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: we know Aviation is going to be the big bar on the Pareto, right? We get back to 2019 levels, which we think we can do. ... We know how to do that. We just have to do it. You put that together, that $6-plus billion of op profit.
finding: Makes Aviation the largest building block of the group cash target and commits to returning it to 2019 profit levels.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: the simple math here to get to a high single-digit free cash flow margin is getting back to revenues in line with where we were pre-COVID, call it, $85 billion to $90 billion. And take the middle of that high single-digit range of 8%, you get to $7 billion.
finding: Turns the vague high single-digit free cash flow aspiration into a checkable figure (~$7B on $85-90B revenue).

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: You need to lead a lean transformation from the front. It's got to be hands on. Nothing is too small to matter, right? Days count. Hours count. The details matter.
finding: Leads hands-on and in detail, and will not hand the operating transformation to consultants or staff.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: 37,000 commercial engines out there in our installed base. Over 60% haven't seen their second shop visit, so there's a lot of opportunity here as these planes are put back in the air.
finding: Builds the Aviation value case on the young installed base and its coming shop visits, i.e. the aftermarket annuity rather than new-engine sales.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We see the LEAP cutting emissions by 15%, being part of that track record of innovation. And as the industry wrestles with its commitment to halve carbon emissions by 2050, we think we're going to be well positioned to do that, not only with LEAP, but technologies to come, be that sustainable aviation fuels, hybrids and the like.
finding: Frames LEAP's 15% emissions gain as the start of a technology path (SAF, hybrids) toward the industry's 2050 goal, i.e. sustainability as the next basis of engine competition.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We're honored to be under wing both at Airbus and at Boeing and work very closely with each OEM to make sure that as they think about not only production rate expansion from here, but also new platforms, that we're well positioned to help them where we can. So I'll let Guillaume and Dave talk to production levels.
finding: Treats both airframers as customers, defers to their CEOs on production rates and positions GE/CFM for any new platform rather than commenting on rate plans.
trigger: Analyst asked for his reaction to Airbus's production announcement the week before.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We're encouraged by our second quarter cash performance. And we're raising our full year Industrial free cash flow outlook to $3.5 billion to $5 billion while our outlook for organic revenue growth, margin expansion and adjusted EPS remains unchanged.
finding: He raised 2021 cash guidance mid-year and then exceeded it ($5.1B industrial FCF), showing a conservative-guide, beat pattern in 2021.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: At Aviation, CFM secured a new agreement with IndiGo to provide 620 of our fuel-efficient LEAP-1A engines with a multiyear service contract. This is one of the largest deals in CFM's history.
finding: CFM's LEAP-1A position on the A320neo is defended in head-to-head airline campaigns. He bundles engines with long-term service contracts to lock in the aftermarket.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: But keep in mind as well, USM doesn't happen to GE Aviation. We're an active consumer, user of USM as well. So it will help us in some respects, lower our costs with respect to the delivered services we provide our airline customers.
finding: He sees used serviceable material (USM) as both a threat and a cost lever for GE's own shops. This hedged view of the aftermarket shapes how GE competes for spares.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: And if the deleveraging and the operational improvements were really jobs 1 and 2, what that progress sets us up for us is frankly spend more time playing offense, first and foremost, organically, be it in improving our commercial execution, putting more money to work smartly in new product development
finding: Explicit priority stack: 1) deleverage, 2) operational improvement, 3) offence, with organic NPD and technology first and bolt-on M&A after.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: The recovery, which we still think from a narrowbody perspective is a '23 dynamic, widebodies in '24, is what we simply can't sit back and wait for, right? We've got to make as much of our own luck as we can. ... improving the turnaround time on our shop visits creates a little bit more room
finding: Culp does not wait for the market. He acts on controllables, such as shop turnaround, to capture recovering demand early, and repeats the 2023 narrowbody / 2024 widebody recovery forecast.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
