quote: We'll see how high, but we'll take that slow, steady improvement from here as opposed to waiting for some sort of spike that may come, but we're really not planning for that.
finding: He plans on a gradual aftermarket recovery and treats any spike as upside, not plan.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: It's probably a little bit of an offset given some of the delays in the 787 program that have been discussed, right, from an AD&A perspective and aviation.
finding: He treats Boeing's 787 delivery delays as a cash-timing issue for GE (airframer deposits), noting it matter-of-factly without criticism of the airframer.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Admittedly small, but the strategic logic behind it, the value-add, operationally, our $3 billion high-performing Ultrasound business will generate and the high single-digit returns we think we will have in time, that's what we should be doing more of in concert with what we're going to do organically.
finding: His M&A template is a small bolt-on with strategic fit, operational value-add and a high single-digit return 'in time'.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: almost without fail, the next day, right, a commodity, a supplier, a logistics provider that we thought was good for the next 6 weeks or the next 6 months offers up a revision to that outlook. So I think I've used a phrase I probably shouldn't, but I'll repeat it. It really is akin to playing Whac-A-Mole, right?
finding: His recurring 'Whac-A-Mole' metaphor for supply chains signals that he expects persistent, shifting disruptions rather than one fix.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: And it's not our style to try to build back a better headline here.
finding: He declines to massage headline numbers, even when supply issues distort them.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: By the end of the week, we had improved processes for welding and quality checks on midframe parts, improvements that we're convinced will help us reach our goals for military on-time delivery by the middle of next year, if not earlier.
finding: Dated commitment: military on-time delivery goals by mid-2022. In February 2022 he admitted process issues, and in February 2023 that 2022 military revenue disappointed and leadership had changed. The commitment was missed.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: let's just take for simplicity's sake, 8% on a revenue base akin to where we were in 2019, right? That pencils out on a $85 billion to $90 billion revenue base to, say, $7 billion of free cash. ... you get close to, let's call it, $10 billion of op profit, convert that to, net of interest and taxes, at 90%
finding: He shows the arithmetic behind the $7B 2023 FCF target (8% FCF margin, about $10B operating profit, 90% conversion), with Aviation as the main profit engine. It is a transparent but later-missed build.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Very pleased with the shop visit activity being up 40% in the third quarter, better than we had anticipated. I think we were calling for up 25%.
finding: Aftermarket forecasts proved conservative: Q3 2021 shop visits rose 40% against the 25% he had called.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: John Slattery, the CEO of GE Aviation, and I joined our Military team in Lynn, Massachusetts for the full week, while our business CEOs joined their teams across the globe. Lean is fundamentally about going to Gemba, where the real work is done
finding: The group CEO and the Aviation CEO spend a full week on the shop floor. 'Go to Gemba' is a personal management habit.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We just wrapped up our annual strategic reviews with nearly 30 of our business units. These complement our quarterly operating reviews, but have a longer-term focus as we answer 2 fundamental questions: What game are we playing? And how do we win?
finding: Strategy is set bottom-up in annual reviews of about 30 business units, framed by two standard questions.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: it's what, $380 billion of backlog, 70% of that's in Aviation. Virtually, all of that is in services. So certainly, a competitive space. But between the catalog pricing dynamics and some of the escalation protection, we think we're well positioned. But we take nothing for granted there.
finding: He sees the aviation services backlog as inflation-protected through catalog pricing and contract escalators, but competitive.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: So there's a lot to come. We're going to be spending. And we're going to be spending smartly in and around those areas to launch technologies that ultimately transition into product programs as our airframer and airline customers deem appropriate.
finding: He commits R&D money to RISE technology now, but ties the timing of an actual engine launch to airframer and airline demand. Technology readiness comes first; the product launch follows the airframe.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: First is greater focus, which will allow these businesses to relentlessly prioritize where they can add the most value and continue to deliver for our customers. Second is more tailored capital structures and capital allocation frameworks that are aligned with each company's distinct strategies and industry dynamics.
finding: Rationale for the three-way split: focus, plus capital structures and allocation tailored to each industry. For aviation this means a pure-play engine company.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Several years ago, we set out to improve our financial position and strengthen our businesses, and financial strength was our priority. ... GE is on track to reduce debt by more than $75 billion by the end of this year and is now on track to bring its net debt to total -- net debt-to-EBITDA ratio to less than 2.5x in 2023.
finding: Explicit leverage ceiling: net debt/EBITDA below 2.5x by 2023, with debt cut by more than $75B by end-2021. In February 2023 he reported over $100B of total deleveraging.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Scott, I think in terms of asset sales, there's nothing planned. None of the steps that we've laid out here are predicated on asset sales. I would reiterate, though, that part of the opportunity to further deleverage the company will come through monetizing the stakes as we have shared previously, both in Baker Hughes and in AerCap.
finding: He funds further deleveraging by monetising financial stakes rather than selling operating businesses. The Baker Hughes exit was completed by February 2023.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: In 2021, we expect to deliver about $5 billion of industrial free cash flow at the midpoint, adjusted, of course, for the discontinued factoring for the full year. We now expect in today's portfolio of businesses to reach high single-digit free cash flow margins or more than $7 billion of free cash flow in 2023.
finding: Headline commitment: more than $7B of FCF in 2023, repeated through April 2022. It was walked back to 'below our prior view' in July 2022, and January 2023 guidance for GE excluding HealthCare was $3.4-4.2B.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Near term, we're focused on delivering top line growth, profitability and cash generation in line with 2019 levels. Long term, through the cycle, we expect market growth of low to mid-single digits with an operating margin in the high teens to 20% range, while converting more than 90% of our free cash flow.
finding: Through-cycle targets for the standalone aviation business: low-to-mid single-digit growth, high-teens to 20% operating margin and more than 90% FCF conversion. 2022 margin reached 18.3%.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: it's probably at this point, a 12- to 15-month undertaking. So when we say early '23, I think that's the best time frame. If we can move more quickly, rest assured, we will. But we want to get it right.
finding: He committed to an early-2023 HealthCare spin with a stated 12-15 month build, prioritising getting it right over speed. It was delivered on 3 January 2023.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We have more than 37,000 commercial engines and over 60% haven't seen their second shop visit, a tremendous opportunity as the market recovers. ... we're investing in lower carbon technologies, such as the CFM RISE program, where we're aiming to improve fuel efficiency by at least 20%.
finding: Culp's aviation case rests on harvesting the young installed base's aftermarket, and on CFM RISE (at least 20% fuel-efficiency gain) to defend the next narrowbody cycle.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I'll serve as Non-Executive Chair of the Healthcare company upon the spin-off. I'll continue as Chairman and CEO of GE until the second spin-off, at which point, I'll leave the GE Aviation-focused company going forward.
finding: Succession plan at announcement: Culp stays GE Chairman & CEO through both spins, with John Slattery continuing as GE Aviation CEO. The transcript prints 'leave'; context indicates 'lead'. In July 2022 he took over as CEO of GE Aerospace himself.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: we're currently planning for improved GE CFM departures, which we expect to average down about 10% off '19 levels and total year shop visits to be up about 20% year-over-year. We expect revenue will increase more than 20% driven by strong worldwide shop visit growth and the ramp of LEAP engine deliveries.
finding: 2022 Aviation commitment (revenue +20%+, shop visits +20%) was delivered: 2022 Aerospace revenue rose 23%, internal shop visits rose over 20% and margins reached 18.3%.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: we're expecting organic revenue growth in the high single-digit range; organic margin expansion of 150 basis points or more; adjusted EPS of $2.80 to $3.50 a share; and a range of $5.5 billion to $6.5 billion for free cash flow.
finding: This group-wide 2022 guide was missed: low end by April, EPS cut to $2.40-2.80 and FCF to about $4.5B in October. Actual FCF was 'nearly $5 billion', below the original floor.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: our customers have worn through a good bit of the green time capacity that they had as they prepare for what I think many of us expect to be improved conditions before too long here in '22 and then going into '23. ... we're talking months, not years.
finding: He reads airlines' exhaustion of 'green time' (deferred overhauls) as a near-term shop-visit catalyst. He expects any variant-driven delays in months, not years.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We're being more disciplined in the projects we choose to underwrite in the broader markets where we participate. This means lower volume with lower risk today but better margins and less risk over time. ... It's okay not to compete everywhere
finding: He trades volume for lower risk and better margins and accepts the revenue hit, which cost 3-4 points of growth.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: A large acquisition in '22, I think at this point, I wouldn't rate that as a high probability. If for no other reason, then we want to make sure we get the spins out and comfortably with investment-grade capital structure, right? That's job one. ... don't be surprised if we rerun the BK Medical way in 2022.
finding: No large M&A during the break-up. Only small bolt-ons are allowed, with investment-grade balance sheets as the gating priority.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I love the fact that GE Aviation is the world leader in commercial propulsion full stop. ... We won't try to be all things to all people. But with respect to aviation and aerospace, I think we'd be open to that. But first things first, I want to make sure we see our way through this recovery
finding: For the aviation-only GE he is comfortable with commercial-propulsion concentration. He is open to adjacent aerospace M&A, but only after the recovery and spins.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: People get caught up in are you spending enough the X percent, Y percent of sales. I don't think that's really the way you drive innovation. At the end of the day, you really have to be close to customers.
finding: R&D philosophy: spend is driven by customer-backed opportunities, not R&D-to-sales ratio targets.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Yes. Well, to be clear, it was not an update. So if I went there, we were reiterating what we thought we had made clear and stated explicitly. I don't think we were convinced that everybody heard us, so we just wanted to get up on the soapbox and shout it a little louder.
finding: When investors miss a warning, he re-issues it more loudly (a pre-conference 8-K style reminder) rather than let expectations drift. He signals bad news early.
trigger: investor expectations too high for H1 2022

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I hope we've never framed that as a ceiling, right? But I'd much rather deliver on a midterm target than necessarily raise that until we've demonstrated we can do that. That's just me, maybe it's wrong, but that's me.
finding: Culp's personal guidance rule: do not raise a medium-term target (Aviation margins of high teens to 20%) until it has been delivered. Demonstrate before promising more.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Early in, let's say, the lease life cycle, those new units are still money losers for us. Not outrageous, but we're probably not breakeven on the LEAP until, call it, 2025.
finding: Dated commitment: LEAP original-equipment engines stay loss-making, though 'not outrageous', until about 2025 breakeven. A year later he still described them as money-losing.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We're never going to do, regardless of how healthy the balance sheet is. First things first, if a team is consumed with the day job right? And you might argue in renewables, by and large, that's what '22 is going to be about. We really aren't going to ask them to do anything incremental or inorganically.
finding: M&A rule: a business still fixing its operations gets no acquisitions, however much balance-sheet capacity exists. Operational readiness gates growth moves.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: These are not supplier issues. So we're not going to point the finger at anybody other than folks in the mirror. ... We haven't tried to muscle our way through this to just get some engines out a little bit more every quarter. ... We need to fix at root cause. And if it takes a while, it takes a while
finding: On military engine delivery problems he accepts slower output to fix root causes rather than force near-term shipments, and takes ownership internally.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We're poised and we know that particularly with the CFM56 fleet, we're going to see a lot of shop visit activity. We're already seeing those sequential improvements as we speak. So unless something happens with the next variant that throws this recovery into jeopardy, we think that's really an execution challenge for us as opposed to demand.
finding: He diagnoses 2022 aviation risk as GE execution (shop capacity, supply), not demand, and puts the burden on GE.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: So a lot to do, lot to do operationally, which really is job one at GE here in 2022 while we get ready for the spin. So we talk about that every day because we don't want anyone to think the spins are more important than delivering 2022.
finding: He insists operational delivery outranks the break-up workstream, to stop management attention drifting to the spins.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I grew up in a neighborhood for 25 years where high cash conversion was considered a good thing. ... And I will not apologize to anyone for my zealotry on this topic. At the heart of a lean transformation, and that's what we're doing at GE, you've got to get it right with respect to your material flows.
finding: Cash conversion and inventory turns are a personal conviction from his Danaher years. Material flow is the link between lean, cash and customer lead times.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: So we just want to make sure that people know that whether it'd be a strategic decision like that or just more disciplined underwriting, we're not going for share. We're not going to try to post the biggest organic revenue number out there if it doesn't carry good margin and good cash potential along with it.
finding: Culp states plainly that share and revenue growth are not goals. Business must carry margin and cash.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: So you may have seen the announcement we made earlier this week at Airbus relative to a hydrogen demonstrator. We also recently announced a program with NASA relative to high-grade electric propulsion. ... We don't know how that plays out. I'm not sure any of us do. ... We want to continue to lead in the next generation of propulsion
finding: Culp spreads next-generation propulsion bets across partners (an Airbus hydrogen demonstrator, NASA hybrid-electric, Boeing/United SAF). He admits the winning technology is unknown but commits to leading whichever wins.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: And when you've got an aviation business positioned where it is in the early stages of a recovery, your cash receipts are going to run ahead of earnings for a little bit. And again, I think that's an attractive part of the GE model.
finding: He values the long-term service contract model because cash leads earnings in an aviation upturn. This supports a services-led economic logic for engines.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: we've got a number of new platforms being launched, be they in Cypress platform in onshore wind, Haliade-X even in offshore, which not unlike a new gas turbine or an aircraft engine don't have peak gross margins at launch, right? So we need to come down that experience curve, which we will.
finding: He treats low launch margins on any new platform, including an aircraft engine, as normal and recoverable through the learning curve.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: particularly with one of our customers, there has been, let's just say, some volatility in deliveries. So it was a bit of a tailwind last year. It's a headwind for us this year. ... as we get the MAX and the -- primarily the MAX on a more normal production and delivery schedule, we'll be talking about this a lot less.
finding: He describes Boeing's MAX delivery volatility diplomatically ('one of our customers') as a timing swing in GE's airframer deposit (AD&A) cash. He expects it to fade as MAX deliveries normalise.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I think all of these CEOs, myself included, and the teams would love to reinvest more, right? ... Being able, day in, day out, to bring down labor, material overhead costs, to make sure our G&A is being deployed smartly just gives us more opportunity, right? To make more bets in Mohamad's shop
finding: Culp links cost-out directly to funding more engineering bets 'in Mohamad's shop', i.e. Aviation engineering under Mohamed Ali: lean savings are recycled into R&D.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Again, no change, mindful of it. There are a host of things that we do not know relative to the situation in the Ukraine, too many uncertainties, and it's probably premature to try to incorporate that today.
finding: Two weeks into the Ukraine war he held guidance unchanged rather than pre-emptively cutting, stating uncertainty openly. He moved to the low end six weeks later.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: when we talk about results with respect to lean, it's safety before quality, quality before delivery, delivery before cost. Cost is important particularly in this inflationary environment, but that is not an acronym, it's a priority set that we are striving to make instinctive in our company on a regular basis.
finding: Explicit priority ordering for trade-offs: safety, then quality, then delivery, then cost (SQDC). Cost comes last.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: all the while continuing to make the longer-term technology bets, be it in CMCs, be it in superconducting generators, to make sure that GE does as it has for over a century, and that is lead in technology.
finding: He funds long-horizon materials and propulsion bets (ceramic matrix composites, electric machines) alongside near-term new product development.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: And that simply means running the business from the bottoms up because it's the 30 P&Ls that deal with customers every day, not those of us in Boston. And that's been a mindset shift, one that has served us well.
finding: Decentralisation principle: decision rights sit with about 30 P&Ls close to customers, not corporate headquarters.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: As Scott Strazik shared last month, our financial results here have been unacceptable, but they are fixable.
finding: Bad-news formula: call the results unacceptable, then assert they are fixable under proven leadership.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: if we just take the $5.5 billion, it doesn't really take us much to get to that $7 billion figure we've talked about for next year. Again, I think Aviation is moving forward in this regard. And the AD&A headwinds we've talked about for this year, probably $0.5 billion shouldn't repeat next year.
finding: In April 2022 he reaffirmed the $7B 2023 FCF and said the AD&A headwind should not repeat. By January 2023 the $7B had been walked back and AD&A was again guided at a $0.5B outflow for 2023.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Many of you saw at our aviation facility in Greenville how our team performs complex machining operations and detailed inspections on high-pressure turbine blades. Here, we're focused on reducing the site's blade delivery lead time. ... These actions have reduced lead time by more than 10 days, and we're targeting an additional 10-day decrease.
finding: He uses visible lean wins at engine-component plants (HPT blades) to show how GE adds capacity without capital.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: A significant marker was the combination of GECAS with AerCap. This move provided us with more than $30 billion, accelerating our debt reduction efforts, which have now totaled more than $87 billion over just the last 3 years. This progress is enabling GE to play more offense like never before
finding: He exited aircraft leasing (GECAS) to fund deleveraging and refocus GE on industrial aviation. He frames deleveraging as the precondition for 'playing offense'.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We've also suspended our operations in Russia, with the exception of providing essential medical equipment and existing power services to the people in the region, and continue to work closely with the proper authorities to ensure compliance with sanctions
finding: Response to the Ukraine war: he suspended Russian operations quickly except essential humanitarian services, and noted limited exposure of 1-2% of revenue.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: All of the GE engines, the CFM International and the Engine Alliance engines that we manufacture and service today can operate with approved SAF. ... we are continuing to work on developing next-generation engine technology that offer the potential to achieve at least a 20% additional improvement in fuel efficiency compared to today's state-of-the-art single-aisle aircraft engines.
finding: His decarbonisation path is twofold: SAF compatibility of the existing fleet, plus a next-generation single-aisle engine (RISE) targeting at least 20% better fuel burn than LEAP-class engines.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: With sustainable demand and readiness across the entire system, were aligned with both Airbus and Boeing and are ready to support our airline customers as well. ... Regarding the specific question on Boeing 737 MAX, we'll continue to have close coordination with Boeing and our airline customers on aircraft deliveries, return to service of the existing fleet and future production schedules.
finding: Culp treats both airframers as aligned partners. On the 737 MAX he gives no independent view and defers to coordination with Boeing on deliveries, return to service and rates.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: But opportunities will present themselves with respect to the stock itself. And you saw the Board authorize back in March a $3 billion buyback. We've been in the market here of late. We think that's a good investment, a good return opportunity for the GE shareholder.
finding: Once deleveraging was largely done he began opportunistic buybacks, justified on return grounds.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: you've heard me say before, we -- I think the first thing I do when I wake up is look at the global departures number. We're north of 80% at '19 levels. Clearly, a narrowbody-led recovery.
finding: Signature habit: global departures are his lead indicator for the engine aftermarket, checked daily.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: So I think our macro view here is really unchanged insomuch as we think narrowbody departures are back early next year in line with '19 levels. Widebodies are coming. I think we're up -- 70% of where we were in '19, but it's probably going to be '24 until we see widebodies at the '19 levels.
finding: Dated forecast: narrowbody departures back to 2019 in early 2023, widebody in 2024. In February 2023 he reported departures still high single digits below 2019 and pulled the widebody return forward to around end-2023.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: When you boil lean down to its basics, it really is about focusing on the customer, a maniacal pursuit of waste and the elimination of waste and an unrelenting prioritization. ... the approach here is not to put together a to-do list, it really is a hands on, let's get it done, let's get it done today
finding: His management system is lean: customer focus, eliminating waste, ruthless prioritisation, a fast hands-on cadence and a bias to act now.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: This is really an approach, top-down, that is hands-on ... I'm headed off Sunday to Wales, spend a week actually on a Kaizen team myself. Now I won't add a lot of value in that environment, but I'll help set a tone relative to this being important, and I'll learn a lot about the business.
finding: Culp leads by personal example on the shop floor. He spends full weeks on kaizen teams (Wales MRO, Lynn) to set the tone and learn the business first-hand.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: But this is an environment where supply chains are so rattled. It would be easy to pull up and say, "Let's not implement pull right now," right? "Let's do that when things are calmer." That's not the mindset. The mindset is this really works.
finding: Under stress he stays with the operating system (pull and flow) rather than reverting to expediting.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We own it all, right? So we never want supply chain to be code for a finger being pointed at a supplier. ... I'm not sure we've always been anyone's best customer. Not that you aspire to that, but in times like these, really tight, clear links with the supply base is critical.
finding: He takes responsibility for supplier performance and admits GE's past behaviour as a customer was poor. He is resetting supplier relationships around clearer signals and partnership.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: On the services side, about 1/3 of that business is under long-term service agreements, the rest is really open market activity. And in our long-term service agreements, we have built-in escalators. ... the rest of the aftermarket is, if you will, more traditional, where we've been able to take up list prices, reduce discounts, add surcharges, look at terms
finding: Aftermarket pricing playbook: escalators in long-term service agreements, plus list-price increases, discount cuts, surcharges and terms on transactional spares.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: remember, with our CFM56 engines, roughly half or 10,000 of them haven't seen their first shop visit yet. So this is still early days in our view. We know that both of our major airframer customers have significant ramps in front of them. We appreciate the underwing positions we have on those platforms.
finding: His aftermarket thesis rests on the CFM56's unvisited fleet and CFM's sole-source/underwing positions on the A320 and 737. He expects retirements to stay muted.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: we have a number of technologies which we would intend to demo by mid-decade. You mentioned hydrogen. We've got hybrids. Certainly our unducted fan engine as well. ... if you talk to the airframers, you talk to airlines, you probably have different views as to how they see that portfolio of options, and those views evolve over time.
finding: For the next engine, Culp keeps a portfolio of technology options (SAF, hybrid, hydrogen, open fan under RISE) to demonstrate by mid-decade. He leaves the choice open because airframer and airline preferences are unsettled.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: The early projects are going to be challenging for us, right? Breakeven is probably a good way to think about those projects largely because we are new. We're just beginning to come down the experience curve. And as a newcomer, I think we didn't necessarily get the best Ts and Cs 1 year or 2 ago.
finding: He recognises that entering a market with a new product forces poor contract terms and break-even early projects, a known cost of new-entrant launches.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: this is not some sort of merit badge to earn, but it really is the way we're going to run the businesses. ... And at every opportunity, I can help coach somebody up, teach them. Or perhaps if they're not with us, right, take that into account as we think about the evolution of the organization.
finding: Adopting lean is a condition of leadership: he coaches leaders, but those who do not adopt the system are moved out.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Andy, I think what we had indicated back in April is that we would see another approximately $400 million off-profit drain in the second quarter. Unfortunately, it played out in just that fashion, but we thought we'd see second half a reduction in that drain, approximately $600 million first to second half. Again, that's not happening unfortunately.
finding: When a promised second-half improvement fails, he says so directly on the next call and quantifies the miss. This is a 'reset and own it' pattern.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We continue to trend toward the low end of our 2022 outlook on all metrics except cash. Working capital will be pressured as we protect customers from the impact of supply chain challenges as well as the timing of renewable energy-related orders, which together are likely to push out approximately $1 billion of free cash flow into the future.
finding: He resets mid-year by signalling the low end and a roughly $1B cash push-out. Protecting customer deliveries with inventory is put ahead of hitting the cash number.
response: guide to low end; cash below range

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We still expect to deliver significant year-over-year improvement in both profit and cash, but below our prior view. With the world evolving so quickly, we have to see how the next 6 months unfold and expect to provide you our 2023 outlook in the usual time frame at fourth quarter earnings.
finding: This walks back the November 2021 / March 2022 commitment of more than $7B FCF in 2023 to 'below our prior view' without a new number, and defers formal guidance to the normal cycle.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: This is an industry that was nearly mothballed that is working very hard to come back to meet ultimate leisure and business travel demand, and we're very much a part of that industry and have our version of those challenges. But we're on it.
finding: Culp frames the post-COVID supply crunch as an industry-wide consequence of near-mothballing in COVID, and owns GE's share of the problem rather than blaming suppliers.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We recently allocated an additional 20% of our existing engineering team to help solve these issues faster. ... We're partnering with our suppliers holding kaizens at points of impact in their shops to help them reduce setup time, eliminate constraints, optimize transportation and improve overall flow to us.
finding: Concrete supply-chain playbook: redeploy about 20% of engineers to delivery issues and run kaizens inside supplier shops. Supplier throughput rose 30%+ in some cases.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: John, Russell, Amy and I were all in Wales at our GE Aerospace MRO facility, where we overhaul both the CFM56 and GE90 engines. As we work to improve turnaround time for a steep CFM56 ramp, the kaizen focused on increasing overhaul capabilities from 3 to 4 engines per week.
finding: Culp personally leads shop-floor kaizens on CFM56 overhaul capacity with his top team. Turnaround improved by 3-5 days.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: The team and I spent time with our airframer and airline customers at the Farnborough Air Show just last week, talking about the need for predictability and stability across the entire ecosystem. We need to do better to deliver for our customers, and quality and delivery are our top priorities.
finding: He admits under-delivery to airframers and names quality and delivery, not cost or margin, as Aerospace's top priorities during the ramp.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: What matters most is the customer. And for sure, the spares in the aftermarket helps us financially at a time like this. But we don't want to have that in any way dilute our focus on shortening cycle times and improving on-time delivery, right? We know our major airframer customers need more engines from us than we are providing
finding: He refuses to let high-margin spare-parts sales crowd out OE engine deliveries to Boeing and Airbus. He openly concedes that GE is short-shipping the airframers.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I'm thrilled to now be leading a very talented team at Aerospace including John Slattery, who has been named Chief Commercial Officer; Russell Stokes, now leading Commercial Engines and Services, Amy Gowder, leading Military Systems; and Rahul Ghai, who will join us next month as the business' CFO.
finding: In July 2022 Culp took direct operating control of GE Aerospace while staying GE Chairman & CEO, and reshuffled the top team. Slattery moved to commercial, Stokes to Commercial Engines & Services, and Ghai came in as CFO.
response: CEO takes direct charge of Aerospace

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We now expect 125 to 150 basis points of operating margin expansion and $2.40 to $2.80 for EPS. This is primarily driven by the higher warranty and related reserves at Renewables this quarter. And aligned with the color we shared in the second quarter, we're expecting free cash flow this year of about $4.5 billion.
finding: Outcome of his January 2022 guide ($2.80-3.50 EPS, $5.5-6.5B FCF): by October he had cut EPS below the original range and FCF to about $4.5B. He attributed the cut to a specific Renewables reserve.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We've been taking a harder look at our operating rhythms, moving toward a more frequent weekly and monthly cadence for each of our P&Ls. This has helped us manage the business in real time and deliver better, faster and more efficiently in what is clearly a dynamic environment.
finding: After taking over GE Aerospace he shortened the management cadence to weekly and monthly reviews per P&L, so the ramp is managed in near real time.
trigger: becoming CEO of GE Aerospace amid the ramp

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Take my 2021 kaizen week team at Lynn. 1 year later, the team has enhanced our closed-loop machining process on the T700 midframe. Now while there's always more to do, this process is delivering close to 100% first-time yields compared to about 50% previously. Real Lean sticks
finding: He follows up publicly on the kaizen he personally joined a year earlier, using its sustained yield gain as proof that lean improvements stick.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: one could argue that it has been the pursuit of scale that has led us in part to our current underperformance. ... It may mean that we don't play in as many markets as we have historically. ... we have no intention of being all things to all people in any of our businesses.
finding: Culp rejects scale and share as goals in themselves. He will shrink a business's footprint to restore returns, a rule he applies 'in any of our businesses'.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: However, like much of the industry, such rapid innovation strains manufacturing and the broader supply chain. It takes time to stabilize production and quality on these new products, which in turn pressures fleet availability. We need to industrialize faster to counteract these dynamics, and we are.
finding: His product lesson: rapid successive technology leaps strain manufacturing and field reliability. New products need time to industrialise, a caution that applies to any new engine.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: But none of the operating actions that we've highlighted here are relying on that legislation. Remember, we didn't think that was going to happen when we talked to you in late July, right? That was a pleasant third quarter surprise. So everything we've been doing operationally is geared toward a lower level of volume, profitability in that context.
finding: Planning rule: size the business and set its break-even for the low-volume case, and treat external tailwinds (here the Inflation Reduction Act) as upside, never as part of the plan.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: At GE Aerospace, continuous improvement is our mantra, and our results reflect our team, our technology and our portfolio's unique positioning as the industry's largest and youngest fleet. ... I hope you see what I see: Strong results, a simpler story and an exciting future.
finding: Signature phrases: 'I hope you see what I see', 'continuous improvement is our mantra' and 'the industry's largest and youngest fleet'.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: And we expect LEAP engine deliveries to grow about 50% in '23. We also expect to deliver profit of $5.3 billion to $5.7 billion and higher free cash flow. Aligned to current airframe or aircraft delivery schedules, AD&A is expected to be about $0.5 billion outflow in 2023.
finding: He gave dated 2023 commitments: LEAP deliveries up about 50%, Aerospace profit $5.3-5.7B, AD&A outflow about $0.5B. He repeated them unchanged a month later. LEAP backlog was almost 10,000 engines and 2022 Aerospace revenue was up 23%.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I think as we look at margins next year -- rather this year, we would expect they would be flat, but the revenue growth will give us an opportunity to drive profit growth up, call it, 15%. ... I don't think we look at 18% as some sort of ceiling that we cannot pierce.
finding: He gives a dated 2023 margin and profit outlook for Aerospace (flat margins, about 15% profit growth) and signals that LEAP maturity should lift margins beyond 18% later.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Our team in Terre Haute produces LEAP turbine center frames and started '22 with about 50 pieces delinquent. Working through multiple Kaizens, implementing flows, standard work and daily management, the team's Lean actions increased output over 20% and improved productivity by about 10%. And today, they are on schedule.
finding: He points to plant-level kaizen results on LEAP parts as evidence that lean, not added headcount or capital, is how GE breaks the ramp bottlenecks.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: when you hear us use the word linearity, right, it gets back to Lean 101. We just want to make every hour of every day count, every day of every week, every week of every month.
finding: Signature operating principle: production and shipments should be linear, not end-of-quarter sprints.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We're laser-focused on supporting our air framers, airlines and lessors as they ramp post pandemic. Today, that means providing stability and predictability for our customers, keeping our current fleet flying and growing our new fleet, all the while continuing to invest in technologies that will define the future of flight.
finding: Culp's operating priority for GE Aerospace is predictability for airframers and airlines. It covers both the installed fleet and new deliveries, with technology investment maintained alongside.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I'm 6 months in leading this business, and my conviction is even higher today that we have a premier franchise ... This starts with the right team. We have a balance of unparalleled experience and fresh perspective with nearly half our leaders new to their roles this year.
finding: Having taken direct charge of GE Aerospace in mid-2022, Culp rebuilt its leadership: nearly half the leaders were new in role. He pairs fresh outsiders with veterans.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: The second is decentralization. For example, in our Commercial Engines business, we're increasingly running our product lines as their own P&Ls, in line with how our customers work with us.
finding: Inside GE Aerospace he pushes decision rights down to product-line P&Ls that mirror customer programmes, the same decentralisation he applied across GE.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I think we've got an ambitious organic R&D agenda at both Aerospace and Vernova. There'll be some situations where I think you'll see us put capital to work to enhance our competitive position. But by the same token, I don't think either business has to fill a gap, fill a hole inorganically.
finding: Organic R&D comes first. M&A is opportunistic, to strengthen competitive position, and he rejects the need for any gap-filling acquisition at GE Aerospace.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I think what we wanted to do first is deleverage to the fullest extent possible. That's why we're so proud of that $100 billion figure I cited earlier. ... we'd really barbell the debt and the other liabilities, meaning Healthcare and Aerospace would carry the load by and large, to make sure all 3 were set up to be investment grade
finding: Deleveraging came first. Debt and legacy liabilities were deliberately loaded onto GE HealthCare and GE Aerospace so that all three companies would be investment grade.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I think our confidence every time we guide Julian is high. We'd be wasting your time and everyone else's otherwise. ... If it turns out to be conservative, great, but that's where we are today.
finding: He presents guidance as high-conviction and openly accepts the 'conservative' label. Beating guidance is preferable to missing it.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We've got warranty expense early on, the CSAs, the rate per flight hour part of that business really hasn't kicked in yet. But that too will reset itself mid-decade.
finding: He gives a dated forecast: LEAP service margins (warranty and rate-per-flight-hour CSAs) normalise mid-decade. Meanwhile Aerospace margin is flattish in 2023 with about 15% earnings growth.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: we do a deep dive at a senior level every week. That's our Tuesday morning review on the commercial side. I think we do Wednesday on the military side.
finding: Culp runs the engine ramp through a weekly senior-level operating cadence: a detailed, centralised review on top of decentralised P&Ls.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: the LEAP A and the LEAP B each have about 2,500 parts a piece and only about 10% are common across the 2 platforms. So there's a lot to manage. ... Again, the environment will become easier with the passage of time, but we can't wait for that.
finding: He frames the LEAP-1A/-1B ramp as a part-by-part complexity problem: about 2,500 parts each, only about 10% common. He will not wait for the supply environment to ease before acting.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: What we've tried to do is avoid the finger pointing. We've tried to avoid the public posturing and just get to work, right? Let's solve the problems. ... We've even moved labor out of our own facilities into supplier facilities to identify the true bottlenecks, the constraints, break them and then ramp from there.
finding: His response to LEAP supply constraints is hands-on: he embeds GE engineers and even GE labour in supplier plants to break bottlenecks, and he avoids public blame of suppliers.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We often talk about shaping the future flight at Aerospace in terms of today, tomorrow and the future. Today is all about supporting the airlines as we see these departure curves continue to improve. ... And when we talk about tomorrow, that's really all about ramping with the airframers.
finding: Culp ranks GE Aerospace's priorities in a fixed time sequence: support airlines' installed fleet today, ramp OE with Boeing and Airbus tomorrow, and fund future propulsion after that.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: our view is there's no 1 supplier, there's no 1 commodity, there's no 1 part of the world that is challenging. ... We're going to control the controllable and work our way through it all the while making sure that we protect and where we can accelerate our investments in the future of flight.
finding: Even in a broad supply crisis, he ring-fences, and where possible speeds up, next-generation propulsion spending (RISE, XA100) instead of cutting R&D to protect near-term results.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We want to maintain that market leadership position. But we've been very direct with customers, we only have so much capacity. We'll work to expand that over time, but we want to make sure our margins and our cash performance are far better than they have been. So it's led to, frankly, a saner price discussion.
finding: With demand above capacity, he uses scarcity to raise price rather than to add capacity quickly or chase share. Margin and cash come ahead of volume.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I think the real pressure that we're focused on, Andy, is with the introduction of the LEAP and as the LEAP ramps ... We know we've got probably 250 basis points of headwind just in the OE side of the house from LEAP. But all those shipments are seeding the next 20, the next 30 years of strong aftermarket performance.
finding: Culp accepts near-term margin dilution from LEAP original-equipment shipments as an investment in a 20-30 year aftermarket annuity. This is the classic installed-base logic of the engine business.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We're deliberately going to bring in more inventory this year than we would otherwise simply to make sure that we've covered our needs given supplier performance, right? So we're going to run heavy just to buy ourselves a little bit of insurance.
finding: Despite his lean and cash focus, he consciously spends working capital on buffer inventory to protect delivery when supplier performance is unreliable. Delivery comes before cash.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: with new units far outstripping the aftermarket for a program so early in its life cycle, we do lose money on those engines. Now we have built the business over decades very much with this model. So we know it's really the price of admission. Not happy with that. We're going to continue to drive toward a breakeven level
finding: Culp explicitly accepts loss-making LEAP original-equipment engines as 'the price of admission' to the aftermarket, while still pushing cost down towards breakeven.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: it's going to be a significant undertaking this year to see our LEAP volumes up 50%. Both GE and Safran are 2 partners of the CFM joint venture are committed to doing that. We've set as much to both our major airframer customers. This is a complicated undertaking.
finding: The LEAP rate commitment is made jointly by the two CFM parents and communicated to both Boeing and Airbus. Culp speaks for the joint venture's output target, not just GE's share.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I think we were disappointed with the revenue numbers that we saw on the military side of things. Last year, we were off to a good start here through the first, what, 7 weeks of this year. But 7 weeks does not yet make a trend, but we've made a number of changes in terms of leadership.
finding: When a unit (Military) underdelivers, he admits it publicly and changes its leadership, while refusing to call a recovery on 7 weeks of data.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: But we can't let all of that activity, dare I say, that pressure, distract us from what we need to do with respect to the longer term, right? It's just so important that we not only protect our investment but also protect our talent that's working on the breakthroughs
finding: Ring-fences R&D money and engineers from near-term ramp pressure.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: But that will be a function of opportunity and where we see growth, profit and cash generation potential as opposed to try to play portfolio manager and shape our portfolio.
finding: Will not reshape the GE Aerospace portfolio for its own sake.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We think by 2025, we should be at a 20% operating margin level, right, so good growth. But we've also got a number of productivity improvements to lay in to be at that 20% op margin ratio.
finding: Sets a 20% GE Aerospace margin for 2025; margins were above 23% by 2024-25.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: the year-over-year pressure that we're going to see as a result of LEAP is about 2.5 points in year on an absolute basis, both from an OE and from a services perspective
finding: Quantifies LEAP's margin dilution and accepts it as the cost of the ramp.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We don't have a birthright on that next order.
finding: Assumes no incumbency right to the next platform; each engine award must be earned.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: It's not about the center. It's about the customer and those closest to the action to serve the customer.
finding: Decentralisation principle: authority sits with those closest to the customer.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: as we've combined our engines and services businesses together, as we've broken out widebody from narrowbody, trying to operate in the way that customers see us.
finding: Reorganises commercial engines into narrowbody and widebody units that combine OE and services.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I had an opportunity to walk a number of our own shops and do the same with some of our suppliers in the first quarter and to see how we're having that impact. But it's still challenging. I don't want to, in any way, suggest otherwise.
finding: Walks shops and suppliers personally and refuses to overstate progress.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We still need to get LEAP both from a new unit and from a services perspective to profitability. That is a mid-decade task for us here in the near term.
finding: Commits to LEAP OE and services profitability by mid-decade; later dated aftermarket 2024, programme 2025, OE 2026.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We, at times, I think, went after business with the best of intentions and didn't get paid for the risks that we were taking, signed up to probably do things that in hindsight we shouldn't have.
finding: Lesson from the Vernova turnaround behind selectivity: do not take risks you are not paid for.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: the RISE program with CFM International. Our 50-50 JV with Safran aims to reduce fuel consumption and CO2 emissions by more than 20% compared with today's most efficient engines.
finding: Frames the next-generation engine as a 50-50 CFM effort with Safran.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: And customers like what they have today with the CFM56, and they want anything that comes online either to replace or augment the 56 fleet to be at that level. And that's not where we are today with the LEAP engine.
finding: Admits LEAP is below customers' CFM56 benchmark.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We wanted to give Scott an opportunity to get his arms around all of that before we were raising our public commitments.
finding: Waits until a leader has a full grip on the business before raising public targets.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: So when you hear some of our customers talk about this not normalizing this year, perhaps towards the latter part of next year. We're working hard to make it happen sooner -- but if it were the latter part of 2024, that would not surprise me.
finding: Forecasts supply normalisation by late 2024; constraints persisted through 2025.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: You've got to embrace that reality, particularly as a CEO because it's not -- it's not something the organization will beat you to, right?
finding: Crisis rule from the dot-com crash, 2008 and COVID: the CEO must confront harsh reality first.
response: Confront reality first, control the controllables, give realistic hope

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Sometimes the benefits of scale and synergies can be a bit of a mirage. And I think that's a truth we have reckoned with.
finding: Sceptical of scale and synergy arguments (said of Vernova's selectivity strategy).

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: And it's not just heavy capital fixed investment that is lacking. In many instances, it's labor. Sometimes it's just arms and legs, sometimes it's frankly experience that left perhaps in early retirement programs, pre-pandemic that didn't necessarily come back.
finding: Diagnoses lost workforce experience and labour, not only capital, as a root aerospace supply constraint.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: is to simply forgo the view that we have to capture every order or that market share is the end-all and be-all objective for the business.
finding: Gas Power and Renewables turnaround rule: market share is not the objective; selectivity over volume.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: we've evolved our product road map such that we're not trying to bring a new turbine to market seemingly every 6 to 9 months. Customers have really embraced our workover strategy. We can come down the learning curve from a quality, from a cost perspective.
finding: In the Onshore Wind turnaround, prefers a few 'workhorse' products refined down the learning curve over frequent new models; a general bias toward derivatives over new designs.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: we're exclusive on the Boeing 737 MAX, and we have over 50% share with the Airbus A320 family.
finding: States CFM's narrowbody position: sole source on the 737 MAX and over 50% share on the A320neo.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Well, I won't speak to competition, Doug. I think that the sheer fact that we're sole source [ underwing ] on the MAX that we have in excess of 50% share when customers can choose on the neo suggests that we've got an enviable market position today
finding: Declines to comment on the rival GTF's problems; points to CFM share instead.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: If customers who haven't had GE [ underwing ] want to come and have a conversation perhaps that they haven't in the past, we would welcome that.
finding: Leaves the door open to win GTF operators without attacking the rival.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: That's not something that Larry Culp, GE CEO, dropped in on the aerospace team or that I came up on my own as the aerospace CEO. We were really -- we put the team in the room and just looked it straight in the eye what are we willing to commit to
finding: Sets public targets with the operating team rather than imposing them from the top.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: And given the long cycle nature of this business, the future isn't Friday, right? It isn't even 2024. There are technology bets that we're making today that will inform aviation in the 2030s and the 2040s.
finding: Frames engine technology as decades-long bets made now.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: we want to make sure that we're really running the company, not from Evendale top down, but from the P&Ls that are dealing with customers day in, day out on up.
finding: Runs GE Aerospace decentralised, from the P&Ls up rather than headquarters down.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: being a function of their performance, not necessarily our readiness because the teams that are focused on the separation work had, I think, real success with HealthCare, are rerunning that playbook here
finding: Times the final spin on the business's performance, not on separation readiness, and reuses a proven playbook.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: we're in deep with both of our airframer customers relative to our own product road map and technology road map for that matter, i.e., RISE, and how we can work together as they evolve their own product strategy. So specifically to the A220-500, I think we'll keep our comments private. We'll have that conversation with Guillaume and his team.
finding: Works engine road maps privately with both airframers and will not speculate publicly on Airbus's A220-500.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: But obviously, as we evolve our product portfolio, we want to be on all the critical platforms that matter in the decades ahead.
finding: Aims to power every major future platform rather than pick sides.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We're taking a similarly disciplined approach to writing new business, like we've done over at Gas, Onshore and Grid with increased rigor on pricing, terms, geographic exposure and other risks.
finding: Turnaround rule: be selective in underwriting, tightening price, terms and risk before chasing volume.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: But we're looking forward to moving beyond deleveraging and playing more offense at Aerospace.
finding: Signals the shift from balance-sheet repair to offence once the spin is done.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We delivered 1,570 LEAP engines, representing 38% growth, yet with more to do going forward.
finding: Reports 2023 LEAP deliveries and immediately flags more to do.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: On a stand-alone basis, including roughly $600 million of corporate and other stand-alone costs, this comes to approximately $6 billion to $6.5 billion of profit and implies flat margins year-over-year, given the growth in LEAP, initial 9X shipments for the 777X platform and other growth investments.
finding: Sets 2024 standalone profit guidance, accepting flat margins from LEAP and GE9X OE growth; 2024 ended about $1bn above the original plan.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Specific to your question, from a LEAP perspective, what we anticipate right now is a 20% to 25% increase in unit growth.
finding: Guides 2024 LEAP deliveries up 20-25%; cut to flat to +5% in July and ended down year on year.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: From a 9X perspective, we do know that, that will be a pressure on us in 2024. We're assuming EIS May of '25, will begin to ship engines in the back half of '24.
finding: Plans on May 2025 777X entry into service; it later slipped beyond 2025.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: But that approach never assumes perfection, right? So we layer in all sorts of checks and audits, process capabilities to make sure that we're doing all that we possibly can to deliver safety
finding: In the door-plug aftermath, stresses layered checks and a safety system that does not assume perfection.
response: Stress the safety management system and layered checks

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: So assume by way of dividends and buybacks, we will return 70% to 75% of our available free cash flow to investors. That will leave 20% to 25% for inorganic investments in the business.
finding: Splits free cash flow 70-75% to shareholders and 20-25% to M&A.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: If we got to a position where we had no other alternative, perhaps we might bring something in, but that doesn't really fit my architecture of strategy first, operational value second and then the financial thresholds last.
finding: States his M&A screen: strategy first, operational value second, financial thresholds last; buys a supplier only as a last resort.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: So we should see operating profit grow more rapidly at a low double-digit rate. And when you pencil that out, that's a $10 billion operating profit number for 2028.
finding: Sets the first 2028 target ($10bn), raised to ~$11.5bn in July 2025.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: The financials obviously matter. But all the while, we want to make sure we're also playing the long game. And that's where Hoshin Kanri comes in.
finding: Uses strategy deployment (Hoshin Kanri) to protect long-term breakthroughs from quarterly pressure.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: But I don't think we won many of those because of price.
finding: Says GEnx 787 wins against the price-aggressive rival engine came from product, not price.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: And make no mistake, we do not judge ourselves on a relative basis. We look at what we've done in the past, we listen to what the customers need, and that's our target. And that target keeps moving
finding: Benchmarks against customer needs and its own past, not rivals.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: a flight safety office that comes up through our chief engineers as opposed to the P&Ls. We like that separation of duties.
finding: Puts safety authority in an engineering line separate from P&L owners.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: But I think, all of us, particularly at this moment, before we talk about rates, always come back to make sure we're doing all that we can on the safety and quality front
finding: After the Boeing door-plug crisis, puts safety and quality ahead of rate talk and defers to Boeing on rates.
response: Safety and quality before rate discussion; defer to Boeing on rates

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: is primarily focused on making sure from a safety and a quality perspective that we are in no way compromising as we think about the wonderful gift we have in the form of these robust skylines.
finding: Will not trade safety or quality for faster ramp.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: if you look at our win rates, particularly in the narrow-body space over the last several years, we've been very encouraged by the sequential trend, the upticks that we have seen there. And we will continue to work hard to earn the business that ought to come our way. No change in that posture whatsoever.
finding: Sees rising narrowbody win rates during the rival GTF's problems but avoids gloating.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: On the LEAP program within CFM International, where we power narrow-body aircraft, reliability and Durability is performing as well or better than its predecessor CFM56 at similar points in their life cycles.
finding: Frames LEAP durability positively against CFM56 at the same age while fixes were still in development.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Thanks go out to the GE team. who significantly improved our financial position, reducing debt by more than $100 billion since 2018.
finding: Claims delivery of the 2018 deleveraging commitment, cutting debt by more than $100bn.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We're also introducing targeted component upgrades into the LEAP-1A fleet that will go into production later this year, and we'll do the same for the LEAP-1B fleet next year.
finding: Commits to the LEAP-1A kit in 2024 (certified end-2024) and LEAP-1B in 2025; the 1B kit later moved to 1H 2026.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: CFM's RISE program is maturing technologies that will serve as the foundation for next-generation CFM engines that could be available by the middle of the next decade. The program goals include reducing fuel consumption and CO2 emissions by more than 20% compared to today's most efficient engines
finding: Positions RISE as the base for next-generation CFM engines in the mid-2030s with a >20% fuel goal.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: our pricing framework is really centered on earning a fair risk-adjusted return on that investment. Our customers have shown over time that they are willing to pay for the value proposition our products offer and on our side, we're focused on being paid for the performance and reliability that we deliver regardless of what our competitors may do.
finding: Prices for a risk-adjusted return on investment and says he does not follow competitors' pricing.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: And I think the updated guide here, the color around LEAP specifically is, is certainly that of high confidence. It wouldn't come out of our mouths. It wouldn't be in our prepared remarks otherwise.
finding: Stakes credibility on the cut LEAP guide; 2024 LEAP still ended below it.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: You'll note that we are adjusting our outlook for LEAP deliveries this year. On a full year basis, we now think we will be somewhere between flat and up 5%, obviously lower than where we thought but still showing modest growth.
finding: Cuts the 2024 LEAP outlook to flat to +5%; by October it was guided down year on year.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: we don't want to turn down the folks that are performing well unduly as we calibrate the ramp rates with those that will, in all likelihood, pace us. So we've taken a view that in some instances, the inventory is in effect and investment with the supply base
finding: Carries extra inventory rather than throttle good suppliers to match the slowest one.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: the common denominator impacting growth across both services and new engines is constrained material supply, with 80% of material input shortages tied to 9 suppliers across 15 supply sites.
finding: Diagnoses the ramp problem precisely to a few supplier sites.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: The airframers that we talk to here at Farn, well, certainly and the airlines as well. No one loves the fact that a new narrowbody order may not be delivered until '29 or '30.
finding: Acknowledges the supply crunch is pushing narrowbody deliveries out to about 2030.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: The GEnx engine offers a 15% lower fuel burn compared to the CF6 and best-in-class time-on-wing, resulting in a 70% life of program win rate on the 87 platform.
finding: Claims a 70% life-of-programme 787 win rate against Rolls-Royce on fuel burn and time on wing.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: delighted to see the LEAP up 4 points from a share perspective. So overall GE narrowbody-powered propulsion is probably north of 70%. So I think the CFM is going to have a longer life in many fleets.
finding: Puts GE-powered narrowbody share above 70% and gaining against rival engines; expects CFM56 to fly longer.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: That is an unlock, Scott but please don't think that it is the unlock, right? It will help, most importantly, because it is part of that durability kit, that matters far more in the spirit of safety and quality than it does delivery.
finding: Plays down a single fix as the answer and ranks safety and quality above delivery.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We're also making progress on LEAP durability with the 1A durability kit, including our upgraded HPT blade and we're expecting it to be certified in the coming weeks.
finding: Promises LEAP-1A HPT blade certification within weeks; delivered at the close of 2024.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: As we said, LEAP will be down, unfortunately, year-over-year in terms of new engine deliveries. But I think we're poised, I think, as Rahul just touched on, to deliver good growth going into 2025.
finding: Concedes 2024 LEAP deliveries will fall, missing the July 2024 guide of flat to +5%, and resets to 2025.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Airbus, obviously, aiming to hit rate 75 down the road. We want to be with them each step of the way. Boeing in a different situation but they're going to be ramping on the other side of resolving the work stoppage as well. And fortunately, they're both going to do that with our engines under wing.
finding: Distinguishes Airbus's steady ramp from Boeing's strike-hit position; CFM wins either way.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: excited about that engine. We know that aircraft is late but every customer that I talk to and have the opportunity to spend time with a few of them just this past weekend, they love the airplane. They want the airplane. It's really, at this point, a matter of time.
finding: Sees the 777X delay as timing, not a demand loss.
response: No change to GE9X test and ramp work; slower ramp

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We would expect leap new units to be up 15% to 20% this year, more to come after that, right?
finding: Commits to 15-20% LEAP delivery growth for 2025; met and raised to above 20% by October.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: So I would just caution anyone to over -- about over-indexing on that, say, that 15% to 20% increase in LEAP newmake in 2025. The demands on the supply base are going to be in excess of that, again because we also need to support the aftermarket with those same partners.
finding: Reminds investors that the same supplier parts feed both OE engines and aftermarket spares, so the two compete.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Again, with flight deck, we can go in and have impact with a lot of our suppliers absent writing an equity check. Have we done that? Will we do some of that? Of course. But I don't think that, that is necessarily a pronounced strategy relative to M&A.
finding: Prefers fixing suppliers through lean help over vertical integration; buying suppliers is the exception.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: But at the end of the day, you're not going to see us as the finger pointers. You're going to see us as the problem solvers. We don't see a lot of value in this company short, that company short.
finding: Refuses to blame airframers or suppliers publicly for shortages; signature 'problem solvers, not finger pointers'.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Well, I never like to think about normalized margins because once you cap a margin target, guess what, you just capped your margin target
finding: Refuses to state a ceiling margin target; continuous-improvement mindset.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I think the framework that we've talked about with respect to aftermarket profitability in 2024 program profitability here in '25 and then OE profitability in '26 is intact.
finding: Reaffirms dated LEAP profitability milestones: aftermarket 2024, programme 2025, OE 2026.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We didn't ship as many leaps last year as we had intended to. We need to make more progress this year, not only with leaps, but really across the engine families.
finding: Owns the 2024 LEAP delivery shortfall plainly.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: A lot of that was reporting into me. I can't be at the center of that as much as I might want to, right? So Mohamed and the team, I think, are off to a terrific start.
finding: Moves from personal hands-on control of the supply fight to a delegated structure.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: So we'd much rather work on the dollars. We get paid in dollars, not in percentages.
finding: Signature phrase: profit dollars over margin percentages.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: the 9X engine, which will be the exclusive engine under wing for the 777X we know we will see pressure, right? And I think we've talked about upwards of several hundred million dollars this year with our volume assumptions. We need to work that hand-to-hand with Boeing.
finding: Accepts several hundred million dollars of GE9X launch losses as the cost of sole-source 777X position.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: But in terms of intent, in terms of alignment, there is no daylight there. Obviously, Kelly and the team of Boeing. I know Kelly be up here in a little bit, are working through a number of different issues, but we are thrilled to be underwing, often exclusively.
finding: Stresses alignment with both airframers and values being sole-source on the 737 MAX and 777X.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Mohamed Ali, 1 of our senior leaders, heads that new team, reports directly to me. And what we've done on the back of the '24 experience is really hardwire 1 team together between supply chain, engineering, quality and a couple of other support functions
finding: Creates a single technology and operations organisation under Mohamed Ali, reporting to him, after 2024's supply problems.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: total engine units were down 6%, with LEAP down 13%. This was lighter than we expected from the slower start to material inputs in January and the lead times to complete new engines.
finding: Owns a LEAP delivery miss in Q1 2025 and ties it to supplier input.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: With those actions, we expect to reduce the tariff costs to roughly $500 million. We're taking additional actions to offset this remaining impact. This includes controlling costs while maintaining investments in key priorities and pricing actions.
finding: Responds to tariffs by mitigating first, then offsetting with cost and price while protecting key investments.
response: Duty drawbacks and foreign trade zones, then cost and price offsets; hold the guide

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Clearly, for the suppliers with whom we've got firm fixed contracts, that additional burden will be borne by them. We'll work through where appropriate, right, adjustments in our overall arrangements with them. Clearly, we've got some bigger suppliers. We've got our partnership with Safran as well, where it's a different dynamic.
finding: Pushes tariff costs to fixed-price suppliers but treats Safran as a partner with different terms.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I don't think we're keen to build out an all singing, all dancing aerospace portfolio just for its own sake. One of the things that served me well over time is making sure that you're strong, not just big.
finding: Signature phrase 'strong, not just big': rejects scale-for-its-own-sake M&A.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: If there's one thing that I would have done differently last year, it would have been to have accelerated the implementation of this technology and operations organization that I mentioned earlier.
finding: Openly names his own slowness on a reorganisation as his main 2024 mistake.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: But we don't have the parts. right? Even if it takes a day to do a shop visit, we're not going to be able to bring those turnaround times down.
finding: Identifies parts availability, not shop labour, as the binding constraint on aftermarket turnaround.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Time on wing, really the hallmark of any outstanding engine platform.
finding: Names time on wing as the defining measure of engine quality.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We know we've got airframers be it Airbus, be it Boeing, others that are very keen to move at an accelerated clip to service their own backlogs. We're gratified to be under wing. That will create a little bit of margin pressure for us.
finding: Accepts OE margin dilution from faster airframer ramps as the price of growing the installed base.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We want the engines to be as robust as possible at launch, but we know there are going to be things that we will be learning and in turn, addressing early in the life cycle.
finding: Accepts that early-life durability issues will be fixed after entry into service, and plans for it.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: the greatest leverage I get as a CEO, the most important decisions that I'm party to are those that pertain to the team, making sure we're recruiting, developing, retaining, promoting the best possible people.
finding: Treats people decisions as the CEO's highest-leverage decisions.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Now subject to Board approval, we're increasing that to $24 billion, including about $19 billion of buybacks and roughly $5 billion of dividends at roughly 30% of net income.
finding: Raises shareholder return plan from $19bn to $24bn, buyback heavy, dividend set at ~30% payout.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Beyond 2026, we expect to return at least 70% of free cash flow annually through a combination of dividends and buybacks. Finally, we're open to opportunistic bolt-on M&A with a high threshold for strategic, operational and financial fit.
finding: Sets a floor of 70% FCF return after 2026 and limits M&A to bolt-ons with a high bar.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
