quote: Operating profit is expected to reach approximately $11.5 billion with margins expanding to more than 21%. And we expect to generate substantial free cash flow of at least $8.5 billion with conversion around 100%.
finding: Sets dated 2028 targets for profit, margin and free cash flow.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: as Safran gets past the labor disruption they had in the second quarter, we're still confident around our deliveries for this year. We've said, previously we'd be up 15% to 20%, no change in that outlook. Here in '25, that puts us, I think, on a path to deliver what, 2,500 LEAPs in 2028.
finding: Holds LEAP guidance despite a Safran labour disruption and sets a 2028 rate of about 2,500 LEAPs.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Since June the 12th, our focus has been and remains on supporting our customers and providing technical support to the regulators. While we were looking forward to a broader update with you in Paris
finding: After the Air India 171 crash he limits public comment to customer and regulator support and postpones the planned Paris investor update.
trigger: Air India flight 171 crash (Boeing 787, GEnx engines), 12 June 2025
response: Support customers and regulators; postpone the Paris investor update; no speculation
lag: ~5 weeks to the first earnings call

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We're not going to go out necessarily and try to upgrade everybody overnight. That will be a multiyear process as the field of engines come in for their next shop visits. So think years, not months in that regard.
finding: Retrofits the LEAP durability fix at natural shop visits instead of a costly fleet-wide campaign.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: And fundamentally, it's all about moving beyond launch, right? LEAP is well into the life cycle now, but it does take time to see that fall through. Typically call it, 8 years thereabouts post an agreement to really see that in the P&L.
finding: Describes the long lag between engine launch pricing and aftermarket profit; patience on payback.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: I think we're encouraged by what we hear from customers, right, witnessed the 60% win rate versus competition. We've got over 1,000 engines now in backlog.
finding: Uses GE9X win rate against the competitor as evidence of market preference ahead of 777X entry.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Plenty of work to do, not only with Safran but all of our suppliers but that's what we're here for.
finding: Names the CFM partner Safran alongside suppliers as a delivery dependency GE must manage.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: So no one breakthrough other than just the relentless application with urgency of our FLIGHT DECK tools deep into the supply base wherever we have a constrained or bottleneck. It's that simple, ain't that hard.
finding: Signature plain-spoken phrase; credits incremental lean work rather than any single breakthrough.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Based on this progress, we now expect to grow LEAP deliveries more than 20% for the full year, up from our prior outlook of 15% to 20%.
finding: Raises the LEAP delivery outlook mid-year once supplier input improves, rather than promising it up front.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: We think that will drive a 2x improvement, I think 8,000 cycles in harsh environments, think 17,000 cycles in neutral environments. So, so far, so good.
finding: Gives specific time-on-wing targets for the LEAP-1A durability kit and reports early field results as on track.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: we're in the certification process on the LEAP-1B equivalent and are expecting to see that come through the pipeline in the first half of next year.
finding: Commits to certifying the LEAP-1B durability kit with Boeing in 1H 2026.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: Our best engineers with our suppliers' best engineers, not trying to negotiate there on the factory floor, but to identify the problem, contain it in the short term and put it in permanent corrective action going forward.
finding: Handles supplier constraints by embedding GE engineers on the supplier floor for lean problem solving rather than commercial pressure.

speaker: H. Lawrence Culp, Chairman & CEO
quote: And through FLIGHT DECK, we're turning strategy into results with a relentless focus on safety, quality, delivery and cost, always in that order.
finding: States a fixed priority ranking (safety, quality, delivery, cost) as the organising rule of the business.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Our financial policy goals remain maintaining a high cash balance, achieving less than 2.5x net debt-to-EBITDA at GE Industrial and less than 4x debt-to-equity at GE Capital, a credit rating in the single A range and reinstalling a dividend in line with peers over time.
finding: Sets explicit balance-sheet thresholds (net debt/EBITDA below 2.5x, Capital D/E below 4x, single-A rating) and puts restoring the dividend after them.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: We estimate the first quarter Industrial operating profit impact from COVID-19 roughly $700 million. Drivers included lower aftermarket sales, project delays and supply chain constraints. This impact is higher than anticipated at the March outlook call, reflecting the rapid global progression of the pandemic, while our prior forecast largely reflected the slowdown in China.
finding: Owns the miss against the March 2020 outlook openly, quantifying the COVID hit and explaining why the earlier forecast was too narrow.
trigger: COVID-19 spread beyond China after the March 2020 outlook

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: We remain committed to achieving our leverage targets, but we now expect to achieve those targets over longer period than previously announced due to the impact of COVID-19.
finding: Resets the timing of the leverage target, not the target itself, when COVID hits; she repeated the line in July 2020, and by Jan 2022 reported 3.3x market-aligned leverage with about 2x expected for end-2022.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: To add a bit more color, COVID-19 represents just over half of the year-over-year margin difference. 737 MAX timing considering install and spare engine volume and supply chain excess costs represent additional 20% of the margin.
finding: Decomposes the Aviation margin decline into COVID versus 737 MAX causes, quantifying each rather than blaming one external event.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: We're targeting more than $2 billion of cost-out this year. ... I can tell you from my experience that as these programs build momentum and the company leaders begin to see how powerful results can be, they tend to extend beyond their stated goals.
finding: Sets a firm cost-out target quickly and expects programmes to overshoot it once leaders see results; GE reported delivering the $2B cost and $3B cash actions in Jan 2021.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: We shipped 472 commercial install and spare engine units this quarter, down 37 versus prior year. Sales of 272 LEAP-1A and 1B units were down 152. And CFM56 units were down 98 units.
finding: In her first quarter she reports the MAX/COVID hit in CFM unit terms (LEAP and CFM56 both down), giving investors the unit drivers rather than only dollars.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: First, keeping our financial position strong and safe with a keen eye on leverage and liquidity as well as cash flow and capital discipline. While GE's actions over the last couple of years have put us on stronger footing ahead of this situation, we will do more.
finding: Her first stated priority as CFO, at the start of COVID, is balance-sheet safety: liquidity and leverage first, then cash flow and capital discipline.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Of course, leverage is important, but liquidity is very important. ... I would also say we expect to have around $20 billion in total credit lines going forward, and that's really in line with our risk appetite.
finding: In a crisis she ranks liquidity above leverage and sizes credit lines (about $20B) explicitly to her risk appetite.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: We continue to hold a liquidity balance covering 12 months of GE debt maturities.
finding: Applies a liquidity rule: hold cash to cover 12 months of debt maturities.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: I have spent most of my career in leadership at lean, decentralized companies. Fundamentally, I believe companies outperform when they have a structure that empowers businesses to take the right actions quickly. This type of structure is critical to respond to situations like we have today with COVID-19 but also to be prepared to pivot to growth.
finding: States a core belief in decentralised decision rights: business units empowered to act fast, both in crises and when pivoting to growth.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: The second quarter was more ... volatile and difficult than normal to forecast. The end market dynamics, especially in commercial aviation, remain unpredictable and, therefore, the outlook for the rest of the year is uncertain.
finding: Declines to give firm 2020 guidance while commercial aviation is unpredictable, saying the uncertainty openly instead of putting a number on it.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: As Larry mentioned, we're targeting more than $2 billion of cost actions and $3 billion of cash actions this year. We realized more than 1/3 to date, and you will see further results in the second half. In total, we expect 1/3 to 1/2 to be structural cost out, which annualizes to $1.5 billion to $2 billion.
finding: Commits to $2B cost and $3B cash actions with a stated structural share; she confirmed in Jan 2021 that both were delivered.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: In addition, but to a lesser degree, we had cancellations of commercial engine orders. This includes 795 LEAP-1B and 22 GE9Xs. Significant, but for context, our ending backlog still has more than 10,000 LEAP-1A and -1B units and 600 GE9X units.
finding: Frames LEAP-1B and GE9X cancellations against the remaining backlog ('significant, but for context'), a recurring way of acknowledging bad news while anchoring on the order book.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Segment margin was negative 15.5% and was heavily impacted by restructuring and charges directly related to COVID-19. These charges included approximately $600 million related to CSA contracts, reflecting lower engine utilization, anticipated customer fleet restructuring and contract modifications and a higher bad debt expense.
finding: Takes a large, front-loaded charge on the long-term service (CSA) book in the worst COVID quarter, reflecting lower utilization, fleet restructuring and bad debt.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: We're making progress here on the more than $1 billion of cost and $2 billion of cash actions. During the quarter, we reduced Aviation headcount by 11% or 5,400 people. Our plan includes a 25% headcount reduction globally.
finding: Responds to the COVID downturn with deep, fast Aviation capacity cuts tied to explicit cost and cash targets.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: I am an industrialist at heart. We operate in important spaces with a great team and leading technology. And we have many opportunities to improve: operations, capital discipline, digitization, using lean to enhance processes and deliver better results.
finding: Presents herself as an operator-CFO whose agenda is operational improvement, capital discipline and lean rather than financial engineering.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: It's $5.5 billion, and it's a liability because basically, it's prepayment for us. And this is largely commercial engines. And the largest portion of this is LEAP-1Bs. ... our risk is sort of limited to refunds on straight-out cancellations. ... So if the airframer agrees to refund progress, also GE and CFM would be required to refund.
finding: Bounds the 737 MAX progress-payment exposure: refunds arise only on outright cancellations, and the airframer leads, with GE and CFM following its terms.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: With our typical seasonality, we expect the fourth quarter to be our most significant quarter for Industrial free cash flow. As Larry said, we're targeting at least $2.5 billion.
finding: Sets a floor for Q4 2020 cash ('at least $2.5B'); the actual was $4.4B, 'well above our expectations', showing conservative floors.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Cancellations slowed significantly this quarter. We saw about 100 LEAP-1B cancellations, much lower than the 800 or so in the second quarter, significant, but for context, our ending backlog has nearly 10,000 LEAP-1A and 1B engines.
finding: Tracks LEAP-1B cancellations quarter by quarter and puts them in context of the backlog, signalling that the MAX order erosion is slowing.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Aviation has completed around 70% of the more than $1 billion of cost and $2 billion of cash actions. To date, the business has realized close to $1 billion in cost savings. We completed further workforce reductions, bringing the year-to-date total to roughly 20%. These efforts have improved our decremental margins to 43% from 59% in the second quarter.
finding: Reports progress on COVID countermeasures against the stated targets and measures their effect through decremental margins.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: in the second quarter, we really took an aggressive look at all our CSA contracts in relation with what happened -- what is happening with COVID and our expectations going forward. So we took a $600 million charge for COVID impact. ... We are, of course, monitoring the sort of current utilization trends and looking at, well, bankruptcies, frankly.
finding: Prefers one aggressive reset of long-term service contract estimates, then holds it while watching utilization and airline bankruptcies, rather than taking repeated small charges.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: So for the year, Aviation margin of 5.6% were supported by significant countermeasures. We realized savings of more than $1 billion of costs and $2 billion of cash actions. This work continues in '21.
finding: Delivers the Aviation COVID cost and cash targets set in mid-2020 (more than $1B cost, $2B cash) and says the work continues.
trigger: Q2 2020 commitment of >$1B cost and $2B cash actions

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: And if we look at the restructuring, we -- basically, we delivered on the $2 billion of cost that we committed to, but also the $3 billion of cash as we promised. And you do have a carryover effect of that going into 2021.
finding: Closes the loop on a public commitment: the 2020 cost and cash targets were met, with a carryover benefit into 2021.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Cancellations were about 400 units, primarily by 1B this quarter, significant. But for context, our ending LEAP backlog still stands at more than 9,600 engines.
finding: Again pairs LEAP-1B cancellations with the remaining LEAP backlog, the same framing used every quarter of the MAX crisis.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: These types of operational improvements have reduced our industrial cash needs to below $13 billion on a go-forward basis. And this creates greater capacity to delever the company. However, we'll continue to hold elevated cash levels through this period of uncertainty.
finding: Lowers the cash needed to run the business through linearity but deliberately keeps excess cash while uncertainty lasts.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Of particular note, we now include restructuring expense for significant and higher cost programs in adjusted EPS and in our segment results. This will drive accountability in managing costs and benefit at the businesses.
finding: Changes the reporting so business units carry the cost and own the benefit of restructuring, using accounting definitions to push accountability down.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: So by combining GECAS with AerCap, we will not only receive substantial cash, but will also ... retain a large stake in a stronger combined company. This gives us a strong upside potential with flexibility to monetize as the aviation industry recovers.
finding: Structures the GECAS exit to take cash now and keep an equity stake to sell into the aviation recovery, rather than selling everything at the trough.
trigger: need to delever and exit financial services

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: So talking about factoring then, we have taken a decision that we will reduce factoring significantly. We have a balance of $7 billion today, and we're going down to around $2 billion.
finding: Makes a one-time structural decision to exit most receivables factoring, accepting a visible $4-5B cash flow hit to improve cash quality.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: In Aviation, we expect to return to '19 free cash flow levels as the market recovers. By then, organic growth in services, cost-out and military growth will help offset headwinds from the introduction of new engines.
finding: Treats new-engine introductions (LEAP, GE9X) as a known margin and cash headwind, offset by services, cost-out and military growth.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: the utilization comes first, and with utilization comes our billing, and therefore, cash, while the shop visit sort of lags a bit on that, right? So that's why we talked about basically flat shop visits in 2021 and then started to see improvements in 2022.
finding: Guides 2021 shop visits conservatively (about flat) on a lag model. She raised this to at least mid-single-digit growth in Oct 2021, and the actual was +10% (Jan 2022).

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: if you start with aviation, we were sort of high-teens op margin before COVID hit. And from what we see and the combination of our actions, including structural cost out strengthening the business, pushing on services and innovation. We do expect to get back to that $4 billion of free cash flow that we had before COVID hit us.
finding: Commits to Aviation returning to its pre-COVID cash level, resting on structural cost-out and services rather than on a market bet.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: So we get a lot of cash now to delever and we have supporting rating agencies both for us and for the combined deal, and we seal that to keep the equity part for -- to really be monetized when the cycle recovers. So I would say all of that had to happen for this to happen now
finding: Describes the GECAS deal as executed only once several conditions lined up (GE's position, the debt markets, rating agency support): she waits for the conditions, then acts decisively.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: So of course, when we compare us and Safran, we don't have exactly the same portfolios, right? We have the narrow bodies, wide bodies, regionals. ... But I would say, if you just compare our assumptions on narrow bodies with there, they're pretty aligned, right? ... So we're not as far off as it can look.
finding: Asked why partner Safran guided more bullishly on shop visits, she reconciles the two partners' views (the narrowbody/CFM assumptions are aligned) instead of moving her own guide.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Additionally, we do not anticipate any further funding requirement for the GE pension plan in the foreseeable future. And by that, I mean the end of the decade.
finding: Extends the no-pension-funding horizon from 2023 (Jan 2021) to the end of the decade after prefunding and the American Rescue Plan Act.
trigger: American Rescue Plan Act and asset returns

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: The Aviation backlog stands at about $260 billion, down slightly sequentially. The largest drivers were Commercial Engines and Services, with approximately 400 LEAP-1B cancellations. For context, our LEAP unit backlog stands at more than 9,200 engines.
finding: Continues to report LEAP-1B cancellations every quarter alongside the remaining LEAP backlog, keeping the MAX exposure visible.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: I would say, when you're down to $2 billion of factoring and off book, then you're on a level which is an effective way for us to use it. Then you're less than 3% of revenue. So I see that as a reasonable and good level for us to keep.
finding: Sets a threshold for acceptable factoring (about $2B, less than 3% of revenue). By Jan 2022 she had gone further and stopped new factoring altogether.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: And I would say, over time, as we earn our right to do this as our free cash flow improves, but also as the business sort of are stable, profitable and growing, then there are also really good targets of acquisitions and integrating them in a successful way, right?
finding: Sequences M&A behind operational health: acquisitions beyond bolt-ons must be 'earned' through better cash flow and stable, profitable businesses.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: So I would say, there's still a lot of uncertainty, and that's why we're holding the low double-digit margin for the year. We need to see the departures, shop visits and customer behaviors really, really play out.
finding: Will not raise Aviation guidance on early improvement: she waits for departures, shop visits and customer behaviour to show in the data first.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: I wanted to say that the AD&A is really about our customers delivering to the end customer, right? And then this is paid out. So that's a good thing. The timing of that is not up to us.
finding: Treats airframer-driven allowance and discount (AD&A) payments on engine deliveries as a timing item outside GE's control, and as a good sign of aircraft deliveries.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Money-wise for R&D, I would say, as a percentage of sales, we accepted -- well, we expect it to sort of continue to be on the 7% to 8%. That is both internal and external funding. And I would say, overall, we do expect also that the third-party funding will sort of continue to increase over time.
finding: Keeps Aviation R&D steady at 7-8% of sales through the downturn, counting customer and government funding and expecting that share to rise.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: as we continue to have the portfolio transition with the introduction of new engines, we get sort of a negative mix. And then over time, we expect the margins to return to high teens, and that would basically give you an op profit of more than $6 billion from Aviation.
finding: Sets a long-range Aviation target (high-teens margin, more than $6B operating profit) while acknowledging new-engine (LEAP/GE9X) mix as a headwind.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: remember, we talked about the Boeing 737 MAX payments, it's about $0.5 billion headwind.
finding: Treats the 2020 Boeing 737 MAX compensation payments as one-offs and flags them as a 2021 cash headwind, so the year-over-year comparison is clean.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: And I would say we took advantage of the urgency that was created out of the COVID. Good companies act fast, right? So we acted fast. And with that, we accelerated GE's transformation.
finding: Uses the COVID crisis as a lever to speed structural change; 'good companies act fast'.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: So I would say we're working on getting the right data at the right level and the right frequency to our business leaders so that together, we can drive the right and the most important decisions with speed.
finding: Her finance doctrine: granular, frequent data pushed to roughly 30 P&L leaders so decisions are made quickly and close to the business.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: And just last week, we announced an agreement with IndiGo to power 310 new aircraft with our CFM LEAP-1A engines. The agreement, one of the largest in CFM's history, includes 620 new installed engines and associated spare engines plus, of course, a multiyear service agreement.
finding: Highlights a large LEAP-1A campaign win that bundles installed engines, spares and a multiyear service agreement, the CFM model of selling the engine with the aftermarket.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: embracing reality and making sure that we have transparency and candor. And I think it's important how you treat people who come sort of with bad news. And I think the critical thing here is really that it's not about the news, it's about what are you going to do about it?
finding: Sets a cultural rule for bad news: reward candour and focus on the fix, not on blame.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: And also the Board started to think about capital allocation motto, what we talked about coming back to competitive dividend and buybacks and then, of course, the redeployment of capital back into the businesses that I mentioned earlier on.
finding: Signals a capital return sequence: competitive dividend and buybacks only after high single-digit cash margins are reached, alongside reinvestment.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: We took out $1 billion of cost in Aviation last year, and we're planning to take out -- we already are taking out more this year, right? ... But exactly when and how that happens, I don't think anyone knows that right now.
finding: Points to cost actions under her control while declining to forecast the timing of the Aviation recovery.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: But Markus, we have to walk before we run, right? So we'll get there first, and then before we get there, we'll talk about the future when we're almost there, okay?
finding: Refuses to guide beyond the current target until it is nearly achieved; she sets new goals only once the old ones are close.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: I would say it's typically higher on new programs because it's earlier on in the engine's life cycle. And that's true for the LEAP as well, right? We've talked about, on average, about 60% of the LEAP fleet on the CSA versus our overall portfolio, which has around 30%.
finding: Shows the LEAP aftermarket model leans on long-term service agreements: about twice the CSA coverage of the overall fleet.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: But if you compare LEAP, you can say that lower volumes means a slower learning curve, although it has a lot of new exciting technologies. And large engine, larger losses, and the margins are impacted as a result of that. I would say that we're really excited about the 777X and the 9X engine.
finding: Acknowledges that lower LEAP volumes slow the cost learning curve and that GE9X carries larger per-engine losses, while staying committed to both programmes.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Aviation service margins are very attractive. And what we had in this quarter was a loss contract, and that's very rare. We have about 200 CSA contracts in our portfolio, and only a couple of them are loss-making. And we're not expecting that impact to repeat.
finding: Contains the bad news: presents the CSA charge as an isolated case in a healthy portfolio and states that it will not repeat.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: We're now targeting mid-single-digit revenue growth for the year, but our high single-digit target remains in place through '25.
finding: Cuts the 2021 military growth target but keeps the multi-year target. By Oct 2021 she said military growth would be negative for the year.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: And based on our 2Q performance, we're now confident that we can deliver free cash flow in the range of $3.5 billion to $5 billion for the year versus our prior outlook of $2.5 billion to $4.5 billion.
finding: Raises the 2021 cash range after a beat, then narrows it in October; 2021 closed at $5.8B industrial on an ex-factoring basis against a $5B jumping-off point.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Looking forward to the second half of '21 and into '22, although inflation pressure is likely to increase, particularly in Aviation and Renewables, we expect the net inflation impact to be limited.
finding: Underestimated 2022 inflation: by April 2022 she said price/cost would be negative net for the year.

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO

speaker: Carolina Dybeck Happe, Senior VP & CFO

speaker: John L. Flannery, Former Chairman & CEO

speaker: John L. Flannery, Former Chairman & CEO
quote: This is really a pivot point for us that this is an execution story going forward. We know what we need to do. We know where we want to go.
finding: At his one-year mark declares strategy settled and shifts the message to execution, with high-certainty language.

speaker: John L. Flannery, Former Chairman & CEO
quote: This essentially completes the announcement or actual closing of our target of $20 billion of dispositions. We've moved on this with deliberation but with an eye for value as well.
finding: Reports delivery of the November 2017 $20B disposition commitment within about eight months, stressing value over speed.

speaker: John L. Flannery, Former Chairman & CEO
quote: Given the ongoing market challenges and related volatility in Power, we anticipate free cash flow will be approximately $6 billion for the year.
finding: Narrows 2018 free cash flow to the bottom of the earlier $6-7B range, blaming Power while holding the rest of the plan.

speaker: John L. Flannery, Former Chairman & CEO
quote: Aviation margins were down 110 basis points on higher LEAP shipments but are up 110 basis points at the half. We expect Aviation margins will expand in the year.
finding: Accepts quarterly margin dilution from LEAP original-equipment shipments while committing to full-year Aviation margin expansion.

speaker: John L. Flannery, Former Chairman & CEO
quote: The team's working through the LEAP launch well. David went through that at the Farnborough show this week in terms of our delivery schedules and being on track with our delivery schedules. They're on track coming down the cost curve as well on a per unit cost.
finding: Defends the LEAP ramp as on delivery schedule and on the unit-cost curve, deferring to David Joyce's airshow account. The slice does not show how deliveries turned out.

numbers.claim: LEAP on delivery schedule and cost curve, Jul 2018

speaker: John L. Flannery, Former Chairman & CEO
quote: The aviation market continues to be very strong. We had a strong orders quarter and a good week at the Farnborough Airshow, with $22.6 billion of wins.
finding: Leads with aviation order momentum (airshow wins) as the offset to Power, using Aviation as the group's stabiliser.

speaker: John L. Flannery, Former Chairman & CEO
quote: We expect earnings and cash pressure in Power will be offset by strength in Aviation and Healthcare and lower Corporate costs.
finding: Relies on Aviation as the earnings and cash offset to Power in 2018 guidance, making it the group's load-bearing business.

speaker: John L. Flannery, Former Chairman & CEO
quote: So when I step back and look at our portfolio of businesses, this one remains a premium business with a very good and visible long-term outlook.
finding: Ranks Aviation as GE's premium asset with visible long-term growth, the business to protect and invest in.

speaker: John L. Flannery, Former Chairman & CEO
quote: We're planning for this to stay at those levels, so we're not looking for any rebound there.
finding: Plans on a trough market persisting rather than betting on recovery, a conservative planning rule for a cyclical business.

numbers.gas_turbine_market: about 50% down over 2 years, planned flat

speaker: John L. Flannery, Former Chairman & CEO
quote: market conditions, they are extremely good in commercial, extremely good in freight, frankly, picking up, good in military. We have a very strong team.
finding: Reads the aviation cycle as strong across commercial, freight and military in mid-2018, the backdrop for continuing the LEAP ramp.

speaker: John L. Flannery, Former Chairman & CEO
quote: We continue to clearly outperform on the orders and with customers and a very strong team running that business with a great execution track record.
finding: Claims GE Aviation is beating competitors on orders and execution, and expresses confidence in Joyce's team.

speaker: John L. Flannery, Former Chairman & CEO
quote: Yes, I'm not familiar with the comment, Andrew, on the Boeing MRO strategy. So that sounds off point to us, but we'll follow up with you on that one.
finding: Dismisses a reported aftermarket-sharing arrangement with Boeing as 'off point' rather than engaging on the airframer's push into engine MRO.
trigger: Bloomberg report of an MRO sharing arrangement with Boeing

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Chief Financial Officer
quote: We have largely completed the investments that are needed to support the ramp of LEAP on the new engine side. And now we are investing to create the MRO shops at capacity. But all of this should keep us within 2 points of revenue and -- CapEx at 2 points of revenue over the next couple of years.
finding: Caps capex at about 2% of revenue, saying LEAP OE capacity is already built and new spending goes to MRO shops.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Chief Financial Officer
quote: So plenty of work to do on cost, and we are all over it.
finding: Signature phrasing on cost ('we are all over it'), which he repeats at the 2024 Investor Day.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Chief Financial Officer
quote: We do expect our new equipment business on the commercial side to be up more than 20%, driven primarily by LEAP, which will be up more than 50% during this year.
finding: Opening 2023 LEAP delivery forecast of more than +50%; by October 2023 he had cut it to +40-45% because of supplier shortfalls.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Chief Financial Officer
quote: Profit growth of $2 billion during this period, both from higher revenue and from improvement in margins that get back to that 20% range by 2025.
finding: Medium-term commitment of +$2B profit and about 20% margins by 2025; the slice shows 2024 margins of 20.7%, so he hit it a year early.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Chief Financial Officer
quote: But there's not a lot of big retroactive fixed cost that we've -- that we need. So a lot of these things that Mohamed is talking about that are quick fixes, they're not going to be a big retroactive cost impact in our financials.
finding: Plays down the financial cost of the LEAP Middle East durability fixes; by June 2023 he described specific warranty and shop-visit reserves taken for such events.
trigger: Analyst question on the LEAP fix for Middle East dust and its cost

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Chief Financial Officer
quote: The recent trends out of China and widebody traffic growth are encouraging. And that could take us through the higher end of our services projections for the year. we want to wait until China and the freight traffic trends become clearer through the year before we revisit this outlook.
finding: Does not raise guidance on early positive signals; waits until trends are confirmed before revising the outlook.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Chief Financial Officer
quote: maintaining cost is a critical element for us. And we are focused very, very sharply on that. So let me start with cost of sales on the left first. On cost of sales, we are expecting to drive 2 to 3 points of productivity every year.
finding: Sets a standing productivity target for cost of sales and makes cost control a core finance agenda.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Chief Financial Officer
quote: 30% of that came from new equipment sales and 70% came from supporting the existing installed base. Not only are the ratios similar for both defense and commercial businesses, they are best-in-class, 2x to some of our closest peers.
finding: From his first investor day he frames GE Aerospace as an installed-base and services franchise and benchmarks its services mix against peers.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Chief Financial Officer
quote: And 9X starts shipping by '25. We start shipping and the volume increases by '25. But clearly, it's an early part of the engine cycle, more OE, no services. So we do expect that 9X will be an issue as well.
finding: Accepts margin dilution from a new widebody engine early in its life as the normal cost of the razor/razorblade model.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Chief Financial Officer
quote: I think we said $2 billion plus back in March. If I said $2 billion, that's an error on my part. I meant $2 billion plus so it's exactly the same number. No change in our outlook for '25 at all.
finding: Corrects his own misstatement on the spot and states that the outlook has not changed.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Chief Financial Officer
quote: these service agreements keep us close to our customer, right? And they allow us to control work scope and also drive a favorable cash profile. ... But if priced right, these contracts can create a lot of value for both our customers
finding: Backs long-term service contracts (CSAs) for customer intimacy, control of work scope and cash, on condition that they are priced right.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Chief Financial Officer
quote: we are committed to an open network, as Russell spoke about this morning because this open network creates competition, drives costs lower and creates options for our customers.
finding: Supports an open third-party MRO network for LEAP, accepting competition in the aftermarket to lower costs and widen customer choice.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Chief Financial Officer
quote: We are following the exact same playbook on LEAP, and there's absolutely no reason for us to sit here and believe that we will not achieve similar results.
finding: Bases the LEAP profit case on GEnx's history (margins up 4x in 10 years) and states it with strong conviction.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Chief Financial Officer
quote: So at CFM, you're right, CFM kind of starts coming down, but the overall revenue for CFM, as Russell showed on his chart, is not that much of a difference between '25 and '28 because you have price increase and other things that go in to cover for the drop in shop visits.
finding: Manages the CFM56-to-LEAP transition by using price to hold CFM56 revenue as its shop visits decline.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Chief Financial Officer
quote: We set up these reserves in the quarter where we established the need to have that reserve and charge that to the P&L. About 2/3 of the reserves that we have on our books today are for these unanticipated, unexpected events that we've encountered since we launched LEAP.
finding: Books durability problems (radial driveshaft, hot-and-harsh shop visits) up front in specific reserves to shield later contract profitability.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Chief Financial Officer
quote: right now, what Airbus is shipping, we're kind of in the 55% to 60% range over the last couple of years. And I think on our win ratio, going back all the way to '21, I think we are in the 70% wins or the awards, I should say
finding: Measures the GTF contest on the A320neo by share of Airbus deliveries and by campaign win ratio, in answer to a question on LEAP's durability lead.
trigger: Analyst: LEAP durability now far ahead of its main competitor; implications for pricing and share

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Chief Financial Officer
quote: But it's just not the increases. It's also the discipline with which we are driving the business so that we're making sure that we are extracting the most out of the price increases that we are putting in place.
finding: Treats pricing as a matter of execution discipline, ensuring list increases are actually realised, not just announced.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Chief Financial Officer
quote: So we've been working to simplify the legacy liabilities, and it's a meaningful step forward in that direction prior to spin. We are approving a settlement program, and that significantly reduces our exposure to future losses.
finding: Chooses to settle legacy tail risks (the Polish bank loans) before the spin rather than carry open-ended exposure.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Larry said it at our Investor Day, and he said, "Hey, if M&A was banned, he wouldn't lose any sleep over it." And I think everybody in the company kind of shares that view ... we'll keep looking at things that make strategic sense, that make operational sense, that make financial sense, but we are at peace with ourselves
finding: Low appetite for M&A: only small tuck-ins that pass strategic, operational and financial tests, with no pressure to do deals.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: we said about 1,700 LEAP ... engines this year and then 2,000 for next year and then growth from that point on.
finding: Committed in 2023 to about 2,000 LEAP engines in 2024; 2024 deliveries actually fell about 10%, and by November 2025 he placed the 2,000 mark in 2026.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: What we've previously communicated, service becomes profitable next year, and I'll come back and speak another word on why. Overall program becomes profitable in 2025 and then OE becomes profitable in '26.
finding: LEAP profitability milestones (services 2024, programme 2025, OE 2026) that he restated each year and reported as met for services in 2024 and on track in 2025.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: clearly, profitability is more important than share. We want to -- if we want incremental volume, we want incremental volume that is profitable and it's profitable.
finding: States a general rule, profit over share, here applied to GE Power but consistent with his pricing stance in aviation.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: On the recent events, it doesn't change much on LEAP for the near term. We are very -- we feel we're in a good market spot right now. So it shouldn't change much for the near term because clearly, we're living in a supply-constrained environment.
finding: Does not expect a near-term gain from the problems of a rival engine maker, since LEAP output is supply-constrained.
trigger: Analyst: 'competitive landscape might be changing' (Sept 2023, after Pratt & Whitney's GTF powder-metal disclosures)
response: No near-term change; focus on meeting airframer and airline demand

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: First and foremost, we do expect both Vernova and Aerospace to be investment-grade at spin, right? So that's kind of priority #1.
finding: Puts investment-grade ratings at the spin ahead of other uses of cash.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: We've made progress on productivity as well. So that's the other part. Not to the extent that we would have liked, but it is progress.
finding: Admits that productivity is behind plan while still presenting it as progress.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: We are now planning for a 40% to 45% increase in fleet deliveries this year, down from our 50% target at the beginning of the year.
finding: First cut to the 2023 LEAP ramp target (from 50% to 40-45%), blamed on suppliers; it set the pattern of LEAP delivery cuts through 2024.
response: Cut delivery target, keep profit guide

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: we implemented a high single-digit price increase this quarter. Now we had pulled forward the price increase from the fourth quarter to the third quarter. So we got a couple of months of incremental price in the quarter.
finding: Pulled the annual spare-parts list-price increase forward a quarter to capture price sooner in a tight market.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: And the rest of that 2-point headwind is coming from incremental R&D to support -- improve -- further improvement in LEAP durability, introduction of 9X and then develop the next generation of products for the future of flight.
finding: Accepts about 2 points of margin pressure to fund LEAP durability R&D, the GE9X launch and next-generation technology.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: it is exactly the steps that we had thought in our minds on how 2024 would look when we were sitting back in March, right? And we had said, hey, '24 will be a step along the way to '25.
finding: Signature 'step along the way' framing, used to place each year on the path to the medium-term targets (again in 2025 for '26 to '28).

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Profit, EPS and cash, all finished above the high end of our guidance.
finding: In 2023 GE beat the top of its own guidance on profit, EPS and cash, showing a habit of conservative guides.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: we are thinking $7.1 billion to $7.6 billion of profit for 2025, which is in line with what we said back in March, just adjusted for the incremental expenses.
finding: Restated the 2025 profit target on a standalone basis; the October 2025 guide was $8.65-8.85B.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: But given the increase in LEAP volumes, introduction of 9x, and the need to create MRO capacity to reduce the turnaround time for our customers, we are increasing CapEx at the higher end of the 2% to 3% range that we had shared earlier. We are being extremely careful about avoiding overcapitalization of our facilities.
finding: Raises capex to the top of a 2-3% of revenue band for LEAP, GE9X and MRO, while again warning against overcapitalisation.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: we aim to distribute about more than 70% of that to our share owners in form of dividends and share buybacks. Subject to Board approval, we will initiate dividend at about 30% of net income. And our Board recently authorized a $15 billion share buyback authorization that goes into effect post spin.
finding: Capital-return framework for the standalone company: over 70% of deployable cash returned, a dividend at about 30% payout and a $15B buyback.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Therefore, we add between $2.5 billion to $3 billion of profit between '25 and '28, getting to approximately $10 billion of profit in 2028.
finding: Set the 2028 target at about $10B operating profit; in July 2025 he raised it to about $11.5B.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: So you won't hear us talk about LEAP being a margin headwind at the overall GE Aerospace levels starting '25. I think that's a big step forward for us as a company.
finding: Committed that LEAP would stop diluting group margins from 2025; in 2025 CES margins expanded while LEAP grew.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: We are, at this point, Rob, we are planning for entry into service in mid-2025. That's the goal. That's the discussion Russell and his team are having with Boeing.
finding: Planned 777X/GE9X entry into service for mid-2025; by July 2025 he tied peak GE9X losses to entry into service and said 'we are still expecting that to be in 2026', and in November 2025 he deferred to Boeing on the 777X schedule.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Sometimes our production environment is independent of where Boeing is because they still want the engines for whatever reason. So I think we'll keep working it. But at this point, we are not -- we don't anticipate changing the -- any shipment outlook for 9X.
finding: Keeps the GE9X shipment plan unless Boeing signals otherwise, and does not cut output in advance of airframer delays.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Taking costs out of our business remains a #1 priority for us. Material inflation has been challenging given the sourcing situation in this environment.
finding: Puts cost reduction first among his priorities despite material inflation.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: We are expecting higher inflation in 2024 than we experienced in 2023. But the price escalations that we put in place in '23 would more than offset that. And we will be price/cost positive in 2024.
finding: Sets a firm rule that price must exceed cost inflation.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: you can see that the large pricing on both LEAP and GEnx, those days are behind us. And we are pricing for the inflationary environment that we are in. And as Russell said earlier, we are pricing for the risks that we take, the investments we make, but more importantly, the performance that we deliver for our customers.
finding: Pricing doctrine: no more launch-style pricing on LEAP and GEnx; price reflects inflation, risk taken, investment and engine performance.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Second, while we will always strive for more price, we factored in mid-single-digit growth or net low single-digit net price increases into this framework.
finding: Plans on mid-single-digit gross and low-single-digit net price, while saying he will always push for more.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: So just 10 years into service, LEAP will almost make as much money as its 30-year-old predecessor by 2028. This just speaks to the potential that this program has over time. And LEAP is following the footsteps of GEnx
finding: Makes the LEAP case on lifecycle economics: a new engine reaches CFM56-level profit as its aftermarket matures.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: I think that's the one that we all need to now replicate this playbook that we've had with LEAP on 9x. The initial shipments, bigger engine, lots of new technology ... So I would say that, to me, is the single biggest thing that we need to manage over the next 3 to 4 years.
finding: Names the GE9X ramp as the biggest risk ahead and plans to apply the LEAP playbook to it.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: We embark on the next chapter of this journey from a position of strength. And the visibility and the accountability that comes from becoming a stand-alone public company will only make us better.
finding: Sees standalone-company accountability as a discipline for management.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: low single-digit net given the caps that we have given the revenue-sharing agreement. Again, none of these things are finalized. Russell will work that with his partners at CFM, especially on the narrowbody side, it's a joint decision.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: This more than offset higher inflation investments and a change in estimated profitability on long-term service agreements on a mature platform, which negatively impacted both services revenue and profit by roughly $200 million.
finding: Discloses a roughly $200M hit from re-estimating long-term service contract profitability on a mature engine and absorbs it within the guide.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: We are anticipating reduced LEAP output in the range of 10% to 15% growth, but continue to expect overall equipment revenue growth of high teens from improving wide-body mix.
finding: First 2024 LEAP cut, to +10-15%; it fell to flat-to-+5% in July, about -10% in October, and ended at -10%.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: our 2030 target for LEAP is we do about 60% or so of the shop visits between us and Safran and 40% are done externally. And of that 60%, there will be a mix between CSAs and T&M, but we are actively working to increase the T&M population.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: So it has been a challenge. But again, as Larry said, that is something we've been trying to manage and manage it as appropriately as we can. But the good news is, despite the $1.2 billion of inventory growth in the first half of the year, we still had 120% conversion.
finding: Admits the problem (an inventory build) and then points to an offsetting positive (cash conversion).

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Looking ahead, given the strong results and the momentum in our business, we are raising our profit and cash guidance. We are reducing our revenue guidance given lower engine output expectations. ... This includes our updated full year LEAP output expectations of flat to up 5% year-over-year.
finding: Second 2024 LEAP cut (to 0-5%) paired with a profit and cash raise, since fewer loss-making OE engines help profit.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: The LEAP is tracking better than CFM56 at this stage of the life cycle. We are expecting LEAP performance to be in line with CFM56 performance on the A320s by the end of the year.
finding: Durability commitment for LEAP-1A; in July 2025 he reported LEAP-1A at CFM56 levels for new and overhauled engines.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: But everything that we need to accrue for, we're obviously accruing for and that's kind of built into the guidance. But I want to say that it's not been a material number for us here as we sit in here in 2024.

quote: We are not able to quantify that just yet because we need to work the exact volume assumptions for '25 with Boeing. So we'll come back to it in January.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: This includes continued sequential growth in LEAP deliveries in the fourth quarter but the full year will now be down approximately 10% year-over-year. This guidance assumes ongoing deliveries to Boeing.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: I think, Seth, you are accurate on both counts, right? Our engine output perhaps is not at the level that we'd expected back in March.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: we constantly balance the needs of both our external and the internal network and prioritize the delivery of parts to reduce the turnaround time for our airline customers, be it in our own network or in the external network.
finding: Allocates scarce parts between spare-part sales and its own shop visits to minimise airline turnaround time.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: safe to say that equipment growth will be faster than that of services and will include higher 9X shipments. So that'll likely put some pressure on margins but it is important to keep this flywheel going over the longer term.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: And the key for us is just to continue to work the cost out. And as we shared at Investor Day, we expect about 30% of the cost to come out by the 50th engine, an additional 30% as we get to the 250th engine.
finding: GE9X plan built on a learning curve with explicit cost-down milestones and profitability by about 2030.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: As you know, about 60% north of that portfolio is serviced by us and is in a long-term service contract. So fewer shop visits on the nx side improves the profitability of that program.
finding: Under long-term service contracts, better time on wing means fewer shop visits and more profit, which aligns durability investment with returns.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: The biggest pressure point here in the fourth quarter is our investment in R&D to support the next-gen programs. So that is the biggest driver here. Given the budget uncertainty, we are continuing to invest from our side to make sure that we meet the time lines that the

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: And for the year, we returned more than 100% of free cash flow to our shareholders, including $5 billion of share buyback and a dividend of around 30% of net income.
finding: In the first standalone year more than 100% of free cash flow went back to shareholders.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: For the year, LEAP deliveries were down 10%, in line with our latest expectations.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: In total, we expect another year of low double-digit revenue growth for the company with profit in the range of $7.8 billion to $8.2 billion, up about $750 million or 10% at the midpoint over 2024.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: LEAP services became profitable in 2024. And the program becomes breakeven in 2025, with OE following a year later in 2026. So that was our prior expectation that continues to be our expectation today.
finding: Reports the LEAP services milestone met as committed in 2023 and keeps the programme and OE dates.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Now as we sit here today, as Larry said in his prepared remarks, we're going to add about $2.5 billion of profit in the 2-year period. So that's about 1/3 better than what we thought just 9 months ago.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Now again, that -- our primary objective is to increase our deliveries and we will do what it takes. But with the improvement in deliveries, we do expect that some of the inventory that we've built up will start getting liquidated.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Obviously, as we're coming out of the gate here, most of the shop visits have been internal. As you said, about 90% or give or take were shop, it is that we performed within Safran and GE. The external network is beginning to step up. We have 5 external partners.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Given our operational and financial strength, we continue to expect to deploy over $8 billion of cash to shareholders in 2025 through dividends and buybacks. We remain well positioned to drive significant shareholder returns while continuing to invest in growth, innovation and focused M&A.
finding: Keeps shareholder returns intact during the tariff shock.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: We have not factored in a slowdown in airframer delivery schedules, further tariff escalation or a global recession into our guidance. We remain confident in our ability to deliver another year of strong results.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: we expect roughly $500 million of cost after our operational actions to minimize the tariff impact. From there, we expect to primarily mitigate this remaining $500 million through SG&A cost controls and price increases. We are maintaining our R&D spend for the year.
