speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Given the tariffs in place, we've reduced spare parts and spare engine sales for the year to that region. This demand is not foregone as our customers in China still have needs for services and spare engines, but they may be delayed.
finding: Cuts China volumes in the guide for prudence but treats the demand as delayed, not lost.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: And whatever is left, we'll share that in some way, shape or form through a tariff surcharge. And hopefully, that doesn't -- it's not a permanent thing, and we can take those away as soon as the tariffs end.
finding: Passes residual tariff cost to customers through a temporary surcharge rather than absorbing it.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Operationally, we are performing better than we expected on the January earnings call. But given the macroeconomic backdrop, we are holding our guidance across the board.
finding: Holds guidance despite a beat when the macro outlook is uncertain, then raised it in July once tariff risks eased.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: And really no change, broadly speaking, to the razor-razorblade model. Now wide-bodies are obviously -- those platforms are now profitable at the -- for the OE business.
finding: Holds to the razor/razorblade model while noting that widebody OE is now profitable.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: One, I think you're right, the shop visit prices are going up. And that's just basically the end of launch period pricing, right? ... But as we think about that price increase that we put in place, that takes a few years for it to show up in our P&L
finding: Raising LEAP shop-visit pricing after launch, accepting a multi-year lag before it reaches earnings.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: At the same time, we are stepping up R&D investments, to improve lead durability, support the GE9X ramp and advanced technologies supporting the future of flight.
finding: Raises R&D for LEAP durability, the GE9X ramp and future technology (RISE) within the 2028 plan.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: But also, we are maintaining some conservatismness around departures that Larry mentioned in his prepared remarks, which impacts our expectations for spare part sales in the second half.
finding: Builds deliberate conservatism into the second-half guide even while raising it.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: higher revenue will support double-digit profit growth, with profit reaching approximately $11.5 billion in '28. ... Our updated outlook from profit and free cash flow, both represent a raise of $1.5 billion versus our prior outlook.
finding: Raised the 2028 targets by $1.5B each (profit to about $11.5B, free cash flow to about $8.5B).

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: These actions give us confidence that we can navigate the impact from CFM56 retirement and that LEAP will not only equal CFM56 profit by the end of the decade, but the profitability levels will continue to improve beyond that.
finding: Moved the LEAP-equals-CFM56 profit date from 2028 (March 2024) to the end of the decade, partly because the CFM56 is lasting longer, and promised further improvement beyond that.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: So the retirements have been trending extremely low. But as you would expect that, hey, as the fleet ages, this should pick up, right? And that's been our expectation. And now we've been proven wrong on that one before.
finding: Openly admits that past CFM56 retirement forecasts were wrong.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: So we'll move -- start moving past kind of peak losses which we expect a year after entry into service for the platform, right, which we are still expecting that to be in 2026.
finding: Ties GE9X peak losses to a year after 777X entry into service ('still expecting that to be in 2026') and now says the programme turns profitable 'into the 2030s', against 'by 2030' in October 2024.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: The majority of this increase is due to trapped inventory, material we purchased, but can't yet use because we don't have all the parts needed to complete a shop visit or deliver an engine.
finding: Explains about $3B of inventory build as trapped by missing parts and sets a goal of at least one more inventory turn by 2028.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: So the material delivery environment is expected to remain tight. We're not expecting that this magically gets better.
finding: Plans on supply remaining tight and does not assume a recovery.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: And even with Leap shop visit volume growing at a 25% CAGR through 2030, we expect CES margins to stay at current levels as we are offsetting the impact of LEAP with better performance on other platforms.
finding: Manages portfolio mix so that lower-margin LEAP aftermarket growth is offset by mature platforms.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Our goal is to more than double the number of LEAP specific repairs by '28. For context, we've developed nearly 3,000 repairs over the lifetime of the GE90 program, and we are targeting a similar number for LEAP at maturity.
finding: Invests in repair development to cut LEAP shop-visit cost (repairs cost about 50% of new parts).

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: So now as you think about '26 specifically, we take the different pieces of our business on commercial equipment, sufficient backlog extends multiple years, as Larry said, in his prepared remarks, we kind of sold out through the end of the decade.
finding: Engine production is sold out through 2030, so the constraint is supply, not demand.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: So we have enough experience with these long-term service agreements that we can do this. We can do it right. We're conservative in how we model it.
finding: Comfortable with fixed-price long-term service risk because of experience and conservative modelling.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Today, CFM engines power approximately 75% of industry's narrow-body flights. This year continues to increase as the LEAP fleet is expected to grow roughly 3x by 2030.
finding: Frames CFM's narrowbody dominance by share of flights, which keeps rising as the LEAP fleet triples.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: So what's built into our assumptions is that both Airbus and Boeing kind of reach their stated goals over the next couple of years, 3 to 4 years.
finding: Bases the CFM56 aftermarket outlook on Airbus and Boeing reaching their stated rate goals.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: I mean you think about where Boeing and Airbus, the benchmark that they are putting on in the market. And so expectations, it will be up 50%, 60% from where we are in terms of total aircraft output in the next 3 years or so.
finding: Plans engine supply against the airframers' published rate targets (aircraft output up 50-60% in about 3 years).

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: And then as we get into -- as you think about specifically on the '26 growth, we don't expect a repeat of the '25 performance.
finding: Lowers expectations ahead of time after an exceptional year.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Given the strong year-to-date performance and trajectory entering the fourth quarter, we are raising our full year guidance across the board.
finding: Second raise of 2025 (after holding in April and raising in July), consistent with a guide-low, raise-later pattern.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: productivity is a plus, but we're facing inflation. We have the 9X losses. So we expect kind of margin expansion opportunities to be limited here.
finding: Accepts flat 2026 margins to absorb the GE9X ramp and inflation.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Well, I think Jay is going to be here, right? I think he's here tomorrow, so I'll let him kind of talk to it, what Boeing is saying. But as far as we are concerned, we are continuing to ship.
finding: Does not comment on Boeing's 777X schedule and speaks only to GE's own shipments.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: This year, we grew probably in the 17 -- [ 1,750 ] range. We expect another 15% to 20% growth rate next year. So that puts us in the 2,000-engine range that we've guided to.
finding: The 2,000-LEAP mark, promised for 2024 in September 2023, is now guided for 2026.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: 1B, we expect certification in the first quarter of next year, so early 2026. we'll get 1B there. Again, now 1B has flown fewer cycles than 1A.
finding: Dated commitment: LEAP-1B (737 MAX) durability kit certification in Q1 2026.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Well, we -- it's always better to be closer to the finish line and further away. So obviously, when we gave guidance $11.5 billion, we were expecting $8.2 billion, $8.3 billion of profit in '25. Now we are at $8.7 billion, $8.8 billion.
finding: Tracks progress against the 2028 target and reports 2025 ahead of plan without raising 2028 early.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: So nobody really believed in the signal we were giving. And we were not standing behind that signal as well because we were making rapid changes. So there was lack of transparency and there was lack of consistency in our behavior.
finding: Owns the 2024 supplier breakdown: GE's own inconsistent demand signals made it worse, and the fix was a stable, shared demand signal.
response: Stable demand signal and engineers at suppliers

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Every morning, at the beginning of every shift, there is a daily standup, right? ... So it's bringing in a daily disposition versus a quarterly target or an annual target.
finding: Prefers daily operating management over managing to quarterly or annual targets.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: FLIGHT DECK is not only helping us improve our own operations, but also its driving improvements across the suppliers, which improved our material flow in the third quarter, material flow was up more than 30% year-over-year
finding: Extends lean (FLIGHT DECK) into the supply base to unlock material flow.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: So we have 550, 600 engineers at our supplier sites at any given point in time. So we work hard with them on problem solving
finding: Embeds hundreds of GE engineers at suppliers to fix their constraints directly.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: what makes GE different, GE Aerospace different, Peter, in my mind, is our 78,000-engine installed base, which is the largest in the industry by far.
finding: Names the installed base as the core competitive asset; aftermarket revenue drives the strategy.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: And then 9X, given the -- even the cost per engine is going to come down, this increase in volumes, that will more than double our losses on the 9X platform that we're experiencing this year. So that's a headwind as we think about '26.
finding: Keeps ramping GE9X deliveries even though rising volume more than doubles losses.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: LEAP now for Airbus, which is a LEAP-1A engine, has now similar levels of performance for everything new that we are shipping out of our factories as the CFM56.
finding: Reports the LEAP-1A durability commitment as met.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: And we're also retrofitting all the LEAP-1A engines with the same durability kit when they come in for the shop visit. So it doesn't drive incremental shop visits.
finding: Retrofits durability kits at scheduled shop visits rather than in a costly fleet campaign.

speaker: Rahul Ghai, Senior VP & CFO
quote: When you come to our factories, if it was a good day, you'll see green. If it was a bad day on any of these 4 metrics, you'll see a red. And that's what happens when you come, when I go, when Larry goes, there's nothing to hide.
finding: Values a transparent culture of visible management, where problems show up rather than being dressed up.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: And look, I just think we have the luxury to be selective and extremely disciplined on where we go, and the capital's going to be allocated to the best returns.
finding: Presents capital allocation as returns-ranked and selective, with large discretionary cash.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: It's still probably as high or the highest returning stuff we do. ... So it's an 18-month payback type of thing, still, yes?
finding: Ranks restructuring among the highest-return uses of cash, with an 18-month payback rule of thumb.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: Appliances, we plan on selling. Again, I think you've heard me say that at least 5 outlook meetings that we plan on selling Appliances. So maybe all these years, I'll be right.
finding: Uses self-deprecating humour to acknowledge a long-repeated commitment that had not been delivered.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: And the extent to which we do M&A, it's going to be bolt on. The synergies are going to be obvious. It's going to be additive to our EPS goals.
finding: Promises only bolt-on M&A; within a year he announced the Baker Hughes combination with $7.4 billion of GE cash (2016-11-03 call).

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: If you look at, let's say, historic margins on product, they've been, let's say, 8-ish percent over time. They're 5-ish today.
finding: Acknowledges product margins had already eroded before LEAP shipped; by May 2017 he said they were about 1%.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: Aviation. Great backlog, unbelievable backlog, good service strength. Military ... we're not counting on any upside there. It's really, in terms of -- it's all about the LEAP. ... And again, we think this is a business that even with the LEAP it's going to be able to grow gross margins and grow margins for the year.
finding: Commits that Aviation will grow margins in 2016 despite the LEAP entry-into-service drag.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: And then on free cash flow conversion, we're trying to get up a couple of points from 85%, up into the high 80s next year.
finding: Targets high-80s cash conversion for 2016; it came in at 80-85% and the longer-run goal later moved between 95% and 80-90%.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: And it doesn't take a lot of organic operating profit growth industrially to get to above $2, right? If you -- it's just arithmetic.
finding: Presents the $2 EPS 2018 target as near-mechanical arithmetic; by May 2017 it had become the high end of a range.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: We got Alstom closed. Appliances is disappointing, but we've got lots of alternatives for Appliances, and we kind of march on.
finding: Treats a blocked divestiture as a setback to route around rather than a reason to change strategy.
trigger: Electrolux appliance sale terminated after regulatory opposition (Dec 2015)

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: In Aviation, it's all about learning curve. Look, I review all these engine launches on a very regular basis. When I look at the dashboard for the LEAP, it is so much better than the dashboard for the GEnx in terms of how we're approaching the learning curve, how well prepared we are for the LEAP launch.
finding: Personally reviews engine-launch dashboards on a regular basis, a hands-on CEO approach to LEAP cost and readiness.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: And we kind of look at those and say, "Okay, now, if there's a big enough gap, do we do it ourselves? Do we do a COE kind of -- what's the approach? What would it take to invest in that business? What's the returns on those investments and things like that?"
finding: Decides in-sourcing case by case with should-cost analysis on GE-designed parts, then a return test on investing in-house.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: And then the ability to do engine-by-engine models versus fleet models when you have a CSA. This is going to be billions of dollars of productivity for our service businesses.
finding: Expects modelling of each engine under service contracts to cut service costs substantially.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: LEAP kind of steps in. Everything I see so far, such as the LEAP execution's going to be pretty good. Again, you start at a higher point. But the learning curve gets steeper and down faster.
finding: Expects LEAP to start at higher unit cost than GEnx did but to move down the learning curve faster.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: If you're in the aviation business, you've got this immense backlog. We ought to be combing through and seeing where the margin opportunities are.
finding: Sees the large aviation backlog as an opportunity to pull cost and margin out of committed future deliveries.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: So when you look at LEAP, the H turbine, the Tier 4 locomotive, these are big systems that are going to be around for a long time, and we have to execute those extremely well.
finding: Makes flawless execution of long-life launches like LEAP a top priority.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: If you can generate 1% fuel performance on GE's installed base of jet engines, that gives our customers $2 billion to $3 billion of profit every year. Small changes mean a lot. It's all about the data, and the way we play this one is by getting more value out of our CSAs
finding: Plans to earn more from engine service contracts through data-driven fuel and maintenance gains shared with airlines.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: I think having a stable portfolio in a company where everybody knows exactly what they have to do, that's valuable to you, okay. That is valuable to our investors, number one.
finding: Promises portfolio stability after the GE Capital exit; a $7.4bn Oil & Gas combination followed within a year.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: I put on here the advanced turboprop, right, which is we just got our first launch customer. We'll get half the funding from European governments as we go forward on this.
finding: Launches new engines into adjacent segments only with a launch customer and substantial government co-funding.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: Now Aviation has already done a lot of this. Aviation has created a series of joint ventures. The Avio acquisition gave us depth in gears. So Aviation has kind of proven the point that there are going to be opportunities for us to make smart investments at high returns.
finding: Holds up aviation's joint ventures and the Avio acquisition as the model for high-return vertical integration.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: I think we had to make a choice in 2009-ish, let's say, on the aviation cycle. And that was not a fun time to have to make that choice. But we made the choice. And the fact is, is that we're going to launch the GEnx, the LEAP and then the 9X.
finding: Committed to the full new-engine cycle at the bottom of the 2009 downturn and sees nothing of that size after GE9X (perhaps the turboprop), so the era of megaprojects and peak R&D is waning.
trigger: Analyst asks whether big R&D phase is over

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: So between 1999 and 2003, engine shipments down 20% plus, earnings down, and from 2003 to 2015, those earnings were up 3.5x. And that's because, in those cycles, we invested in technology. We invested in customers. We played through. We flexed cost.
finding: Kept investing in aero-engine technology and customers through the 1999-2003 downturn and credits that with a 3.5x rise in aviation earnings.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: But one thing you won't see is a big IT acquisition. I can guarantee you, you're not going to ... see that because that is the graveyards are filled with people on that one, right.
finding: Rules out large deals outside GE's core competence, preferring equity stakes and partnerships.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: I always look at these product launches as risks as well because you've got -- they're hard to execute. So I didn't think we -- we did not execute GEnx for instance all that well. So we kind of took the lessons learned from the GEnx and applied those to the LEAP
finding: Treats engine launches as major execution risk, admits the GEnx launch went poorly and applied those lessons to LEAP.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: Every business that had gross margins as one of the AIP metrics, hit it. So 2016, everybody's going to have one, right.
finding: Uses annual incentive metrics as the main steering tool, extending gross-margin targets to every business.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: I have a difficult time reconciling this with the mood that is in the markets.
finding: Counters market pessimism with GE's own order and backlog data rather than conceding macro risk.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: there's no one China, right? I don't think macro anymore when I talk about China, I think micro. I think about Aviation, Healthcare, Power, Mining. ... But Aviation is super strong, even today.
finding: Signature 'micro not macro' framing: breaks macro risk into business-level demand, with aviation as the strongest.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: We hit or exceeded all of our goals in 2015. Organic growth was up 3% with 80 basis points of margin expansion leading to 7% organic profit growth. EPS was $1.31, up 17%.
finding: Claims a clean sweep of 2015 commitments.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: Aviation, guys, we're still seeing good revenue passenger miles. There's lots of opportunities for our Aviation business to continue to grow. ... And at the end of the day, I think in an environment like this, this is the ballast for the company, is the installed base.
finding: Views the aviation installed base and passenger traffic as the stabiliser of group earnings in a downturn.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: Every one of our businesses has a very detailed incentive compensation plan that, internally, just like last year, rolls up to more than we talk about externally. And that's the way we've run the place.
finding: Sets internal targets above external guidance and relies on incentive pay to drive delivery.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: it's got to make sense in the context of the world we see today and not the rosiest of projections as it pertains to the future. So we're going to be a disciplined buyer
finding: Underwrites acquisitions on current conditions, not the rosiest projections.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: However, we want to take a more conservative position on the year, posting revenue down 15% to 20% and operating profit down 30%. We will continue to outperform our competitors and capitalize on volatility.
finding: Cuts the outlook for a weak segment while holding the group EPS framework, offsetting it with stronger units.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: We continue to win in the aviation market as the LEAP remains the engine of choice and on track for a successful launch.
finding: Commits publicly to an on-track LEAP launch in 2016; the January 2017 call reported 44 LEAP engines shipped in Q4 2016.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: we have a product cost council that's led by Jeff and Vic Abate and Philippe Cochet. We're tracking all products as they go through the system. There's a lot -- because for instance, as LEAP comes in, GEnx keeps going down the learning curve.
finding: Manages launch margin drag centrally through a product cost council, offsetting LEAP with GEnx learning-curve gains.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: We're tested. Companies who think they're perfect can get you in trouble. GE is not perfect, but we make progress every day.
finding: Uses a short, measured admission of imperfection while framing the company as resilient and tested.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: the insights we're getting into asset performance not for a fleet, but for a serial number. What do we know about that jet engine, how it's performing, how it was configured, how we ought to treat that jet engine in terms of coming off a service?
finding: Pushes engine services toward analytics for each serial number to manage shop visits and service cost.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: in the mid-'90s, we created what we call a long-term service agreement or today, we call a CSA, which was really a breakthrough in industrial services, where we changed the risk paradigm with our customers. And we entered into long-term service agreements, where we bore some of the risk associated with the cost of ownership of those engines.
finding: Is willing to take engine cost-of-ownership risk from customers through service contracts in exchange for long-term profitable revenue.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: we've been very focused on simplification, pushing down authority in our company, faster decision, et cetera, along with fast works and how we think about development, the speed with which we do it, the no-go decisioning that we're doing there.
finding: Promotes decentralised authority and fast go/no-go decisions in product development as a cultural goal.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: I wanted to give you a little bit more context for revenues since our plan is back-end loaded. ... We see organic growth at 2% to 4% for 2016, likely trending close to the bottom end of the range.
finding: Prepares investors for the bottom of the range; growth guidance was cut to 0-2% in October and the year ended at 1%.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: We have a large inventory build behind new NPI with LEAP, H and wind products. These are all shipping in the second half.
finding: Accepts a first-half cash drag from LEAP inventory build and promises second-half recovery.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: Power and Aviation remain strong. They're 60% of our earnings and we see consistent performance year-over-year. They have very strong service franchises, productivity programs and our market positions are growing.
finding: Treats Power and Aviation, both service-led, as the earnings core that underwrites group commitments.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: Orders pricing was down slightly versus a year ago. Power and Aviation pricing was positive, but Oil & Gas continues to be pressured. ... Aviation had another excellent airshow with more than $25 billion in commitments
finding: Points to positive aviation pricing and air-show order volume as evidence of competitive strength.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: Look, I think this is really all about growth and competitiveness in building new business, so I think that's the context for what's we're announcing today.
finding: Deflects a pointed accounting question with a strategic answer rather than engaging on the detail.
trigger: Analyst asks about the new revenue-recognition standard and aircraft-engine OE accounting

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: Dave, when does the advanced turboprop go -- enter into service? ... So that's probably the best example of a new product, let's say, that's being designed fully with additive in mind.
finding: Points to the advanced turboprop as the first engine designed around additive parts for cost reduction.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: We're always going to need suppliers but in places where we think we have very specific expertise and competitive advantage, those are places that as time goes on, we think about making versus buying. ... Avio, of course, we've got a pretty good experience with that.
finding: Applies a make-versus-buy rule: in-source where GE has specific expertise, citing aviation's Avio acquisition.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: We plan to have these businesses report to Dave Joyce in Aviation. While the usage will span the company, David is our biggest practitioner.
finding: Puts a company-wide capability under the aviation chief because aviation is its biggest user.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: I think Avio is the right way to think about LM. We see good opportunities in the supply chain. ... And what we saw on Avio is we are able to keep the non-GE base in Avio. And we think we can do the same thing with LM.
finding: Uses the Avio Aero acquisition as the template for buying critical suppliers while keeping their third-party customers.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: When we launched the Capital repositioning in April of 2015, we established the goal of $2 EPS by 2018. Since then, our outlook for Oil & Gas has worsened ... But all of our metrics for compensation purposes will continue to be linked to $2 of EPS in 2018. We're aligned with investors.
finding: Acknowledges headwinds but keeps the $2 EPS target, defending it by tying management pay to it.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: We've developed a keen eye for what changes through each cycle and position for growth when others pull back. This has helped us gain share in Aviation, Power and Healthcare over time. ... This is the right time in the cycle to invest.
finding: Invests counter-cyclically, citing aviation share gains as proof that moving while rivals retrench pays off.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: We think it makes the company more competitive over the long term. Here again the GE Store adds substantial amount of value, both from a global footprint, from a cost-out standpoint, and we still see a good return in the mid-teens as we think about the investment.
finding: Judges large acquisitions such as Alstom against a mid-teens return expectation.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: the entire team is really committed to execute the $2 bridge by 2018, and I'll give you the details of how we expect to get there
finding: Recommits publicly to $2 EPS in 2018 despite the oil and gas downturn; five months later he recast it as the high end of a range.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: There's 15 parts in production right now. David Joyce is kind of running this play for us. Our goal is to have 500 parts in production by 2020.
finding: Sets a dated additive-manufacturing target, led by the aviation business, for parts in production.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: Flexible contracts. We see from an aviation standpoint, we're going to get probably close to high single digit, 10% organic growth in services and aviation next year, and this is a big piece of that.
finding: Forecasts near-10% aviation services growth for 2017 driven by flexible service contracts.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: From a cash flow standpoint, again, one of our goals is to get 95% free cash flow conversion into the operations. We'll be at about 85% this year, 80% to 85%.
finding: Sets a 95% free-cash-flow conversion goal; by May 2017 he had lowered it to 80-90%.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: But I don't see big chunks coming out of the portfolio, and I kind of like the way the company looks right now.
finding: Signals portfolio stability in December 2016; the break-up came under his successors, after the slice.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board
quote: if you own an industrial company, you always have to sit there and say, "Is this a hobby or is this real?" ... if you do it in power and oil and gas and transportation, 8 separate times you're going to fail. What you have to do is once really well, give it a chance to breathe
finding: Builds new capabilities (digital, additive) centrally once and shields them from the businesses until they are proven.

speaker: Jeffrey R. Immelt, Former Chairman of the Board

finding: Four days after ET302, he puts root cause and corrective action ahead of business messaging and calls passenger confidence the industry's foundation.

speaker: David Leon Joyce, Vice Chair
quote: On the 320neo family, our airline customers are averaging 95% utilization, which is 8.4 points better than our competition. Now let me put this in perspective. The utilization advantage enables any of our airline customers to fly about 120 more flights per year per aircraft
finding: Competes with the Pratt & Whitney GTF on aircraft utilisation and translates it into airline revenue.

speaker: David Leon Joyce, Chief Executive Officer, President and Vice Chairman of GE
role_at_time: President & CEO, GE Aviation; Vice Chairman of GE
quote: In '19, we missed our revenue forecast because of supply chain delinquencies. Orders were there. We just didn't deliver. We're using that capacity created by the LEAP program rescheduling to address these delinquencies.
finding: Owns a forecast miss bluntly and turns freed LEAP capacity into a fix for other late deliveries.

speaker: David Leon Joyce, Chief Executive Officer, President and Vice Chairman of GE
role_at_time: President & CEO, GE Aviation; Vice Chairman of GE
quote: Next up, 777X powered by GE9X entering service in 2021. With that completed, we have successfully transitioned our commercial engine business, including the aftermarket, to a winning product portfolio for decades to come.
finding: Restates the GE9X entry into service as 2021, a year later than the 2020 he gave in March 2019.

speaker: David Leon Joyce, Chief Executive Officer, President and Vice Chairman of GE
role_at_time: President & CEO, GE Aviation; Vice Chairman of GE
quote: We've reduced our LEAP production capacity to 1,400 engines this year while ensuring we can support Boeing production rates for the remainder of this year and into '21 ... And to compensate, we plan to reduce CapEx and OpEx, including a hiring freeze, restructuring and reallocating capacity to other demand that has been delinquent due to the constrained supply.
finding: Responds to the MAX grounding by cutting LEAP capacity and costs while keeping the supply chain able to ramp back for Boeing.
response: LEAP 2020 plan cut from about 2,200 (Mar 2019 forecast) to 1,400

speaker: Kevin G. McAllister, Former Chief Executive Officer of GE Aviation Services and President of GE Aviation Services
quote: The data scientists stood up and said, "Look, I found a correlation between the percentage of takeoffs from higher-altitude airports versus the distress that you're seeing on these parts." ... allowed us to isolate this condition to Carrier A, which means we didn't have to go pull 100-plus engines from the 18,000 engines in the fleet
finding: Pairs engineers with data scientists so that fleet actions can be targeted by data rather than applied to the whole fleet.

speaker: Kevin G. McAllister, Former Chief Executive Officer of GE Aviation Services and President of GE Aviation Services
quote: This chart shows that managing averages does nothing for you. You have to be able to segment variation of fleet so you can get down to actions by airline and by engine ... fundamentally, it's a faster, simpler way to drive decisions deeper into the organization
finding: Rejects fleet-average management in favour of per-engine, per-airline decisions pushed down the organisation.

speaker: Kevin G. McAllister, Former Chief Executive Officer of GE Aviation Services and President of GE Aviation Services
quote: in the Services business, our focus is to move technology back into the installed base, and we do this to give value to our customers in the form of increased time-on-wing and increased fuel efficiency.
finding: Retrofits new-engine technology into the installed fleet to sustain aftermarket value and campaign wins.

speaker: Kevin G. McAllister, Former Chief Executive Officer of GE Aviation Services and President of GE Aviation Services
quote: the TrueChoice Flight Hour agreement, where customers turn over to us over a 12- to up to 20-year time frame maintenance cost on a dollar per hour basis. Now this is a terrific opportunity for us to drive productivity inside of GE by improving time-on-wing and by reducing cost of shop visit.
finding: Takes on 12-20 year maintenance-cost risk in rate-per-flight-hour contracts, betting on GE's ability to improve time on wing and shop cost.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller (header prints Senior VP & CFO; introduced as SVP and CEO of GE Transportation)
quote: one of the challenges we really gave our India engineering team was to really focus on how do we take engineering design to value and should cost and really take product -- our product costs down for this product. ... already, we've been able to, through product cost reduction, add 10 points of incremental margin to the as-bid deal
finding: Wins large tenders and then designs cost out after award, adding margin points to the bid.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller (header prints Senior VP & CFO; introduced as SVP and CEO of GE Transportation)
quote: we invested heavily not only in the technology, but in ensuring that we deliver it at a good cost to our shareholders. The product margin really has been on parity roughly with legacy products, which I think is a very healthy thing.
finding: Judges a new-product launch by margin parity with the legacy product, not technology alone.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller (header prints Senior VP & CFO; introduced as SVP and CEO of GE Transportation)
quote: Look, we compete with Caterpillar. They're a great competitor. They're a great company. And look, that's something where our focus today is all about continuing to bring the best technology, the best digital solutions at the most competitive price and win.
finding: Speaks about rivals respectfully and competes on technology and price rather than attacking them.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller (header prints Senior VP & CFO; introduced as President and CEO of GE Transportation)
quote: A lot of these international deals when we bid them are bid in a competitive tender at quite low margins. We attack product cost ... But these international deals, we're typically able to take them 2, 3, 4x up the curve on our op margin for those deals once we bid them
finding: As an operator she bids competitively at thin margins and relies on later cost-down, the logic of buying engine share and working down the cost curve.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: I'd kind of call it a "back to the basics" approach, consistency and transparency but with data that you can digest.
finding: Signature framing for disclosure: 'back to the basics', consistent and transparent metrics.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Look, there is nothing I have seen that gives me an indication of an accounting issue here.
finding: Defends the contract-asset model; three months later the SEC opened an investigation into GE's long-term service agreement accounting.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: And we expect 150-plus more than last year in LEAP shipments and expect to see moderating spares growth, but based on current year-to-date performance, we expect margin rates will be positive for the total year.
finding: Forecasts Aviation margins positive despite the LEAP ramp; Q4 LEAP shipments rose by 158 and 2017 margins expanded 100bp.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: On cash flow, we now expect Industrial cash flow for the year to be about $7 billion, and that's what Baker Hughes GE reported on a dividend basis post transaction. This is well below the $12 billion estimate we provided at second quarter earnings
finding: Resets cash guidance sharply on arrival; 2017 Industrial CFOA came in at $9.7B, above the reset.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: On the CapEX side, we're running our CapEX at about a 0.9 reinvestment rate as we go into 2018. We've had some major launch investments. You've heard about those, really covering the last couple of years. We've run about a 1.4, 1.5 reinvestment rate over the last couple of years.
finding: Cuts the group capex reinvestment rate below 1x once the engine launches (LEAP and others) roll off, allocating by business cycle and returns.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: And as we go through this process, at this point, I do expect the charge to be more than that. But we do have capital plans in place and we don't expect to have to put GE parent cash into GE Capital.
finding: Rules out parent support for GE Capital; GE then planned about $4B of parent contributions in 2019, including $2.5B paid in Q4 2019.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: David talked about the ramp in the Aviation LEAP engine, so going from 473 this year to close to 1,200 next year. We've got a lot of inventory building in the supply chain right now to make sure we can hit that launch next year and those ramp rates
finding: Funds the LEAP ramp with supply-chain inventory in advance, accepting a working-capital cost to protect the delivery rate.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: these are long-term contracts, typically 10 to 20 years, where our customers have predictable maintenance costs in exchange for performance guarantees on equipment, okay. And for us, it means we are deeply integrated in those customer operations. They are high-margin, high-return contracts.
finding: Sees long-term service agreements (the model for CFM engine aftermarket deals) as the high-return core of the business.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: how we think about expansion of CapEx to support, say, certain engine programs and other things, and making sure we've got the discipline both at the outset but also over the life cycle of how we return that money to our shareowners.
finding: Holds engine-programme capex to a full-lifecycle return discipline governed by a new board capital-allocation committee.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: you saw that we cut the dividend yesterday by 50%. I think we had a dividend to free cash flow payout ratio that was quite high the last couple of years.
finding: Backs a 50% dividend cut as a payout-ratio correction and a move to balanced capital allocation.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: And yet at the same time, Power has had some pretty deep operational issues. Power is fixable. We believe that's over a 1- to 2-year period.
finding: Sets a 1-2 year turnaround horizon; in October 2019 she described Power as 'a multiyear turnaround'.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: As you look at 2018, we laid out guidance for 2018, so $1 to $1.07 of earnings per share, $6 billion to $7 billion of free cash flow.
finding: First full-year guidance as CFO; 2018 closed at adjusted EPS of $0.65 and adjusted free cash flow of $4.5B.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: when I came into that business in October 2015, 30 days in, we were going very hard at restructuring headcount actions. ... I think what you should expect is my style tends to be one of operating here, going deep, coming back up, really making sure the theory is operationalized.
finding: Describes her own style: fast cost action on arrival, deep operational involvement and follow-through.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: One of the challenges we've had in Power is that we had plans that I would say were too optimistic for the market that we were in and we built for those plans.
finding: Draws a lesson against building capacity and inventory to optimistic plans, which shapes her caution on rates.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: you have GECAS, which frankly is largely independent of our Aviation business.
finding: Early in her tenure she called the lessor separable from Aviation; by March 2019 she argued that owning both made each better.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Look, we've got very, very strong positions in Aviation and Healthcare and in Transportation in terms of the end market customers and where our pricing profile is.
finding: Sees Aviation as having pricing power, unlike Power and Renewables.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: But broadly in the GE culture, we need more transparency and candor and pushback. ... Cash and cost is what I used to repeat over and over and over at Transportation, right, cash and cost.
finding: Signature phrase 'cash and cost'; asks for candour and pushback in the culture.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: GE Capital Aviation Services, GECAS, is a strong business and has performed well through many cycles, and it will remain as it is today.
finding: Ring-fences the aircraft-leasing arm while shrinking the rest of GE Capital; by October 2018 she said a sale was something GE 'could think about'.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Now we were in the middle of a process. We did not have a number. And this process, as you can imagine, is very complex. ... And we had said that we would share the charge when we knew it, that's why we're having the call today.
finding: Handles bad news by flagging direction early ('more than' $3B) and calling a special call as soon as the number is final.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: We're on track to meet our delivery commitment of 1,200 LEAP engines in 2018, with a production volume of more than 2,000 engines by 2020. Military is on track for mid-single-digit growth. The team is executing well on cost-out and is committed to holding margins flat despite the steep LEAP ramp.
finding: Commits to the LEAP rate ramp and to flat Aviation margins; 2018 delivered 1,118 engines (short of 1,200) but margins rose 130bp.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Some of the controls that we're implementing are things like just really making sure that we're much tighter on our underwriting, not only how we think about the strike zone around returns but importantly how the cash profile really looks on these contracts going out several years.
finding: Adds multi-year cash profile, not just returns, as a test for long-term service contracts.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: I like to joke and say, "We just need to go be boring for a while." Because when you're really, really great operationally, you're actually pretty boring.
finding: Signature phrase: wants predictable operating delivery rather than headline moves.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: we've gone through fairly deep dives into the different elements of the company. And we have no plans for an equity raise. It's not been discussed.
finding: Rules out an equity raise; through January 2020 GE deleveraged by selling assets and cutting the dividend, not by issuing equity.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: We said we would ship between 450 and 500 engines ... in 2017. We shipped 459.
finding: Cites a met LEAP delivery commitment (2017) as evidence for the next one (1,100-1,200 in 2018).

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: I actually think the way you should want us to think about it is this is an and equation. We need to run our businesses extraordinarily well. That should be a given.
finding: Treats operational fixes and portfolio moves as parallel tracks, not alternatives.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: In the first half of these contracts' lives, we're typically investing in these assets. We're stabilizing technologies. We're launching them in their earlier years and making sure we're really meeting those customer guaranteed uptimes.
finding: Defends service-contract economics as front-loaded investment that pays back later in the contract, as with engines under service agreements.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: we preestablished intercompany supply arrangements at market prices for an extended period, so that they knew they would have access to that supply when they needed it to really help launch the company. We made sure that we had strong definitions around commercial markets as to how we shared them
finding: Her model for partner governance: market-price supply contracts and explicit market-sharing rules set up front, the questions a joint venture such as CFM depends on.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: We're making good progress on our commitment to recover on LEAP deliveries by the end of third quarter and are on track to deliver 1,100 to 1,200 engines in 2018.
finding: Sets a dated LEAP schedule-recovery commitment; it was missed (still about 4 weeks late in January 2019), although the unit range was met (1,118).

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: we're continuing to focus and make progress on our 4 key financial priorities, which are strengthening our cash position in delevering, reducing our costs, driving a cash and returns focus, and finally, to simplify and drive more transparency.
finding: States her first-year CFO priorities in rank order: cash and deleveraging, cost, cash returns, transparency.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: For Aviation engines, we previously recorded revenue using levelized margins for a contract. And under the new standard, engine accounting reflects the revenue and cost for each individual engine. The most significant effect of this change is on our new engine launches, like LEAP.
finding: Moves to accounting that books each new engine at its own cost, bringing the early-programme LEAP losses into view instead of averaging them.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: We've included these in our backlog historically, as our historical experience has shown no net cancellations as any canceled engines are typically moved by the airframer to other program customers.
finding: Treats cancellable engine orders as firm backlog because airframers reassign cancelled slots, a low view of engine order-book risk.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: With respect to Aviation, we've got healthy free cash flow conversion there and that continues to improve as we get into the next couple of years in '20 and '21 as they come down their investment cycle
finding: Expects Aviation cash to rise as the LEAP/GE9X investment cycle rolls off from 2020-21.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: we'll maintain our $0.48 dividend through the date at which Healthcare becomes a separate stand-alone company and the 2 boards will determine their dividend policies in line with peers at the time.
finding: Reaffirms the dividend until the Healthcare separation; four months later it was cut to $0.01 per quarter.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Our financial policy continues to target a net debt-to-EBITDA ratio of less than 2.5x, and we remain committed to having a strong single A rating and a Tier 1 short-term rating.
finding: Commits to a strong single-A rating; S&P cut GE to BBB+ about three months later.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: As you can see, our expected net debt-to-EBITDA at the end of 2018 is approximately 3.5x on about $50 billion of net debt.
finding: Forecasts 2018 leverage; the actual year-end figures were $55B of net debt and 4.8x.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: We are about 4 weeks behind schedule but are making good progress on our commitment to recover on LEAP deliveries by year-end and remain on track for 1,100 to 1,200 engines in 2018.
finding: Commits to recovering the LEAP schedule by year-end 2018; units landed in range (1,118) but the business was still about 4 weeks late in January 2019.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: For the year, the continued challenges we were seeing in Power are putting pressure on our total year adjusted Industrial free cash flow outlook. We currently expect it to be about $6 billion
finding: Gives a point estimate for 2018 cash that she withdrew in October; adjusted free cash flow was $4.5B.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: On the services side, we are seeing some higher turnaround times in our shops just given the volume ramp, which is resulting in higher shop costs. We saw some of that in the second quarter. The team is taking very specific action on that.
finding: Flags shop-capacity strain in Aviation services early and quantifies it as a cost issue under active fix.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Not included in orders are $22.6 billion of wins at list price for GE and CFM from the Farnborough Airshow with engines of about $19 billion and services of about $4 billion. We saw significant activity in key commercial engine segments, including LEAP, with $12 billion of wins
finding: Reports airshow wins at list price, kept separate from booked orders, with LEAP the largest share.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: We have not made any decisions or have plans right now to do anything with GECAS, but certainly that's something. As we think about the timing and the pace of execution on our overall plan, that is something we could think about.
finding: Keeps the aircraft-leasing arm available as a deleveraging option without committing.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: And then with respect to the discussion about an equity raise, I'm not sure we have -- I have anything more to add to what Larry said before.
finding: Defers to the CEO on equity-raise questions rather than ruling one in or out.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: we intend to reach net debt-to-EBITDA of 2.5x. We plan to achieve that over time, with substantial progress through 2020.
finding: Softens the June commitment (<2.5x by 2020) to 'substantial progress through 2020' after the Power reset.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: And we're roughly 4 weeks behind on production as a result of the delays in material, but we remain committed to delivering 1,100 to 1,200 units. Aviation's performance remains on track to deliver 15-plus-percent op profit growth for the year.
finding: Holds the 2018 LEAP unit commitment despite supplier delays; 1,118 were delivered.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: it's clear that, with respect to Power, the issues will persist longer and with deeper impact than we had initially expected, which will cause us to significantly miss our full year cash flow and earnings targets.
finding: Owns a guidance miss outright rather than trimming it.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Peeling back and looking forward, we do see CFM coming down, but it's more than offset by military being stronger, the LEAP cost curve really coming down over the next few years and the services strengths continuing.
finding: Lays out the Aviation profit model through the engine transition: CFM56 OE declines offset by the LEAP cost curve, military and services.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: as of the first quarter of '19, you'll recall that the dividend is decreasing to $0.01 per share per quarter, which will preserve about $4 billion of cash in 2019.
finding: Accepts an almost complete dividend cut to keep cash for deleveraging.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: We asked our new Controller, when he started, to take a clean look at everything across the company. And they -- as they went through their normal standards CSA review this quarter, did pay particular attention to higher-risk contracts
finding: Uses a fresh controller review to reset long-term service contract estimates, taking charges early for a 'realistic view'.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: more than 50% of CFM deliveries will be reduced next year, but the LEAP also ramped from the 1,118 we had this year up to ... 1,800-plus. So that remixing continues to occur.
finding: Plans a LEAP ramp to 1,800+ in 2019; the quarterly shipments later reported (424, 437, 455, 420) total 1,736 after the MAX grounding.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: over the last 2 years, we've taken ... out more than 40% of the cost of the engine and are ahead on the learning curve initially laid out for the program. The overall program will break even around 2021.
finding: Commits to a LEAP programme breakeven around 2021 on the strength of cost-out ahead of the learning curve.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: our credit rating was downgraded from A to BBB+ with a stable outlook in early fourth quarter. This impact has been manageable with less than $15 million of collateral posting and a smooth transition to a Tier 2 commercial paper program.
finding: Reports the downgrade plainly and puts a number on its contained impact.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: And in total, we shipped 1,118 LEAP engines for the year. We're still behind on deliveries by about 4 weeks, but the business expects to be back on schedule by mid-2019.
finding: Admits the year-end LEAP recovery commitment was missed (still about 4 weeks late) and resets it to mid-2019.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: The mixing from CFM56 to LEAP resulted in a margin drag of approximately 160 basis points in 2018 and 130 basis points in the quarter. The business is successfully offsetting this margin pressure through continued growth in aftermarket services, military and changing the mix of company-funded R&D spend.
finding: Quantifies the cost of the engine generation change and names the levers that offset it (services, military, R&D mix).

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: The LEAP engine continues to perform very well with a 58% win rate on the A320neo family and 81% win rate in the narrow-body segment when you add in Boeing 737 MAX and COMAC C919. Utilization rates are over 95%.
finding: Measures the competition with Pratt & Whitney's GTF by LEAP win rate on the A320neo, citing it alongside the sole-source MAX and C919 positions.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: We remain committed to our financial policy of targeting a rating in the single-A range and an Industrial leverage ratio of less than 2.5x net debt to EBITDA as well as maintaining a high cash balance.
finding: Restates the financial policy that bounds all capital decisions: single-A rating, <2.5x leverage, high cash.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: While we expect negative free cash flow in 2019, I'd like to underscore that we expect to cross well into positive territory in 2020 with further acceleration in 2021.
finding: Makes a dated cash commitment for 2020-21, set before the MAX impact was known and before COVID.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: And honestly, we are, underneath this, running the businesses to higher numbers. So if you pull it back, different process grounded in reality and, we believe, reflects what we hope is a conservative plan.
finding: Runs the businesses to internal stretch targets while giving external guidance with deliberate conservatism.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: I'll start by noting that EPS is a financial result from our operational management and no longer the metric we manage to. However, we know that it's an important guidepost for our investor base.
finding: Explicitly moves the management metric away from EPS towards cash and operations.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Selling it for more than $20 billion of cash, 7x revenue. So it's, I think, a very efficient transaction to help bring sources into the company to delever.
finding: Sells a prized asset at a high multiple to fund deleveraging, judging the deal by its value as a source of cash.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: I think if you look across our businesses, most of them in this cycle are pretty recession-resilient for the next 12 to 18 months. Aviation continues in a strong cycle. Obviously, we'll see if anything happens with the 737 MAX, but 2019 feels very solid there.
finding: Calls Aviation recession-resilient for the next 12-18 months, a horizon that ran into early 2020; the slice ends in January 2020.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: It is really too early to comment on really any of it. What I would tell you with respect to GE is, on Aviation, we have about 1,200 engines flying on the 737 MAX. With respect to our services contract, cash flows, it's really insignificant for 2019.
finding: Within days of the second crash she sized GE's MAX services exposure as insignificant for 2019; the larger hit came through delayed engine receivables (about $1.4B of 2019 cash).

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: But obviously, Boeing is a huge partner of ours, and we're in the field helping them in any way we can get the aircraft back online.
finding: Positions GE as a supportive partner to Boeing in the crisis rather than distancing itself.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: We're not planning on the market. This is all a self-help story, but could it be higher than that? I think it could be, but we're not, we're not.
finding: Builds turnaround plans only on actions GE controls and excludes market upside.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Our engines are continuing to move to Boeing. And I think, for now, the aircraft shipments are on hold.
finding: Confirms that engine deliveries continued in the first days after the grounding.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: our challenges are really clear here. We've got too much debt at the company, and we're taking actions to tackle that very directly and very swiftly. And we've really got to turn around our Power business.
finding: Names debt and the Power turnaround as the two problems to solve first, in plain language.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: GECAS, which we talked about a little bit ago, is deep aircraft and engine domain, really a leading business in the marketplace. While on one hand, it is not highly integrated with Aviation, we do think it's made better by the fact that we own both companies
finding: Argues that owning a large lessor (GECAS) next to the engine maker adds domain and cycle insight.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: I think the businesses sometimes feel like they don't own it. And so your ability to actually impact the strategy, your ability to touch and manage that cost more directly had become more disconnected.
finding: Explains her reason for pushing shared services and IT back into the businesses: ownership drives cost and strategy.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Last year, we shifted our 2 key incentive comp metrics to be 50% free cash flow, 50% earnings, and that is exactly the same as it is this year.
finding: Pays the business leaders half on free cash flow, which makes cash a governing objective.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: As we shared at the outlook call, total engineering effort, comprising both company and customer-funded spending, continues to grow in line with top line growth.
finding: Keeps total aviation engineering growing with revenue while shifting the mix towards customer-funded R&D to protect margin.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: it's consistent with our view over the last year, which has been breakeven in 2021. We do expect -- it ranges depending on the LEAP-1A or LEAP-1B -- more than 10% cost-out this year on the engine. And if you remember, since the end of '16 already, we've taken out more than 40%
finding: Holds a dated LEAP original-equipment breakeven commitment (2021) backed by a cost-out track record.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: Specifically on the MAX, we have not changed our engine production plans at this time. But the timing of cash flows may be impacted by collections of receivables from Boeing, depending on when aircraft deliveries resume.
finding: First full response to the grounding: holds LEAP-1B production and treats the exposure as receivables timing.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: We shipped 424 LEAP engines this quarter versus 186 in the first quarter of 2018. And we finished the first quarter on schedule with Airbus and 2 weeks behind schedule with Boeing. But we expect to be back on schedule in the second quarter.
finding: Reports LEAP delivery slippage to each airframer in weeks and commits to a recovery quarter.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: From a discounting perspective, we do see discounting of both -- across both engines and services. And typically, when we contract on a deal, we will have differences in our contracts with both airframers and with customers in terms of whether it's discounting or timing of cash flows.
finding: Confirms that engine campaigns are won with discounts on both engines and services, with terms varying by airframer and customer.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: the underwriting framework that has been implemented there, I think, has been very helpful as well, more focused on risk-adjusted cash returns and margins, no longer comping on share, just a more balanced risk/return framework there.
finding: Explicitly ranks risk-adjusted cash returns and margin above market share when bidding.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: We believe these decentralized functions are ultimately run more efficiently and with greater accountability when decisions are made at the businesses.
finding: States the decentralisation principle: decision rights and costs belong in the operating businesses.

speaker: Jamie S. Miller, Senior VP & CFO
quote: our first priority is to strengthen our balance sheet. And so in terms of pivoting to play offense, right now we're focused on getting our leverage down, making sure we got a solid and stable foundation for the company and then we'll consider other actions beyond that.
